apps.business_model: A house-banked dice betting game. The user (a player) connects a wallet, funds app-scoped GAS credit, picks one face (1-6) and stakes GAS. The deployed contract (Neo N3 PlatformGame kernel 0x740671b1… testnet / 0xa7840a8d… mainnet; Neo X MiniAppDiceGameEVM 0xFA795F81…) records the bet, requests a Morpheus VRF roll, and on a matching face pays 5.70x the stake out of the house bankroll after a 5% platform fee (EV = 1/6 × 5.70 = 0.95, so a 5% house edge). Risk/custody: the player's stake leaves the wallet to the contract; on N3 it is consumed as credit and only refunded/paid when the oracle callback settles; on Neo X the bet is atomic (a revert returns funds). The house pays the win; the platform earns the 5% edge. The contract asserts house liquidity >= stake × 5.7 before accepting, capping the max payable stake.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → (N3) optionally Fund Stake credit → pick a face → enter a stake within [0.05, network cap] and within max-payable-stake → see the 5.70x payout + net win preview → Roll (signs the GAS-backed bet) → 'Rolling — oracle is settling' pending state → VRF callback resolves: Won (payout to wallet), Lost, or Refunded (stake returned). Money lifecycle: stake → contract; on a post-deposit failure the GAS is held as reusable game credit; settled win pays from the bankroll; the dice/result/history reflect the on-chain DiceBetResolved/Refunded events.

gaps.title: No exit/withdraw for stranded N3 game credit if the roll never settles
gaps.evidence: On Neo N3 a failed/unsettled bet leaves the stake as app-scoped credit: PlayArea shows directCreditBanner 'it funds your next roll automatically' and statusFundsRecoverable 'Your GAS is held as game credit and automatically funds your next roll' (locale/messages.ts:93, :117). But there is NO withdraw affordance — main.tsx only reads getDirectGasCredit and re-spends it on the next placeDiceBet; the resolve loop markUnresolved leaves the bet 'rolling' forever (main.tsx:254, :284). If the Morpheus VRF callback never fires (the live oracle is the dependency), the only 'recovery' is another roll that also won't settle, so the credit is effectively trapped. fogplay/on-chain-tarot/last-survivor all expose a withdraw() exit; dice's frozen kernel does not, but the UI never tells the user the GAS cannot be pulled back to the wallet.
gaps.fix: Frontend copy-only: change the directCreditBanner / statusFundsRecoverable text to state honestly that the credit can ONLY be re-spent on a future roll and is NOT withdrawable to the wallet (no refund path on N3), so the user understands the irreversibility before staking again. If the kernel does expose any per-app GAS-credit withdraw, surface a Withdraw button reading getDirectGasCredit; otherwise label the credit 'roll credit (not withdrawable)'.

gaps.title: UI promises VRF settlement without disclosing it depends on a live off-chain oracle
gaps.evidence: Hero, route panel and locale repeatedly promise authoritative on-chain settlement: 'Morpheus VRF settles the result on-chain' (locale docHowItWorks:18, resolvingBody:127), diceVrfRouteCopy 'oracle callback resolves or refunds the pending roll' (:48). On N3 the resolve loop polls for up to 36×5s then silently markUnresolved (main.tsx:263-284). A first-time player is led to believe settlement is guaranteed/near-instant, when on N3 it requires the configured oracle signer to call back; if that signer is offline the bet sits 'Rolling…' with no resolution and no refund surfaced beyond the (non-withdrawable) credit.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: before the player commits on N3, surface a short trust line in the bet panel ('Settlement waits for the Morpheus VRF callback; if it is delayed your stake is held as roll credit until it resolves'), and after the resolve poll times out, replace the indefinite 'Rolling…' with an explicit 'Settlement pending — the oracle has not resolved this roll yet' status plus a 'Check again' action that re-runs resolveN3Bet, so the unresolved state is legible rather than a frozen spinner.

gaps.title: Catalog manifest omits the 5% fee / 5.70x / odds that the in-app UI surfaces well
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json operation_panel 'Roll' description mentions '5.70x after the platform fee' but the top-level description ('Pick a face, preview the stake, submit, and reveal the on-chain result.') and tags hide the odds (1/6) and the 5% house edge from the store listing. The in-app PlayArea does surface all of it (oddsLabel '1/6', feeLabel '5%', rangeLabel, houseLiquidity — PlayArea.tsx:204-225), so this is only a catalog-copy gap.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add the win multiplier (5.70x), odds (1/6), and 5% house edge to the neo-manifest.json description so the economic model is legible at the catalog/listing level, matching what the play area already shows.

apps.business_model: A single-player, house-banked coin-flip game. The user (player) picks heads/tails and wagers GAS (0.05–100). The deployed standalone contract MiniAppCoinFlip (testnet/mainnet 0x5d82339d… per neo-manifest; runtime points testnet at 0x23848839…) consumes the prepaid wager and settles the flip ON-CHAIN with Runtime.GetRandom in the same transaction — no oracle, no pending bet — paying the winner 2x atomically from a house bankroll. Economics: 50/50 odds, 2x payout ⇒ 0% nominal house edge on the flip itself (the house's edge/risk is bankroll variance; it refuses any bet it cannot pay 2x). Custody: wager deposited as prepaid credit via memo 'miniapp-fogplay:bet'; an aborted flip leaves reusable credit that is withdrawable via withdraw(account). The house pays wins from bankroll funded by withdrawBankroll/onNEP17Payment.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → choose Heads or Tails → enter/select a wager within the house-payable cap → see the 2x payout preview → Flip (deposit memo'd GAS then flip() in one settled tx, or flip directly if prepaid credit covers it) → instant Won (2x paid to wallet) or Lost result from the Flipped event → stats/history update. Exit/recovery: prepaid credit from an aborted flip is reused on the next bet or pulled back with Withdraw.

gaps.title: Catalog manifest still describes the OLD broken oracle-callback model, contradicting the real atomic contract
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description: 'Fast oracle-backed coin flips on Neo N3. Pick heads or tails, place a GAS wager, and wait for the on-chain callback to settle the round.' and technologies.oracle.enabled=true 'Morpheus Oracle randomness callbacks settle each flip on-chain'. But the deployed MiniAppCoinFlip flip() is ATOMIC GetRandom with no callback (useCoinFlip.ts:11-13, :405), and the in-app manifest.ts/locale were corrected to 'Instant on-chain coin toss', docDescription 'there is no oracle callback to wait for' (locale/messages.ts:43-46). The store listing tells a newcomer to expect a wait-for-callback flow that no longer exists.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: rewrite the neo-manifest.json description to 'Instant on-chain coin flip — Neo N3 native randomness settles each flip and pays 2x in the same transaction', and set technologies.oracle.enabled=false with copy noting Runtime.GetRandom (no oracle), so the catalog matches the corrected in-app copy.

gaps.title: 50/50 odds and 0% house edge are never stated before the wager
gaps.evidence: The arena shows '2x payout' + the computed payout preview (CoinArena.tsx:61-62) and WagerControls shows the house-payable cap, but nowhere is the win probability (50%) or the fact that 2x on a fair coin is an edge-free bet stated. A newcomer sees '2x payout' which can read as favorable without knowing the chance is 50%.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add an odds chip next to the 2x payout preview in CoinArena/WagerControls ('50% chance · pays 2x') using an existing locale key, so the player can reason about EV before committing.

apps.business_model: A two-sided on-chain gacha/blind-box marketplace. Creators publish a machine (MiniAppGasBox, testnet/mainnet 0xeb635b6e…) with a play price in GAS and a weighted prize inventory (name+weight+amount), fund a prize pool that must cover the largest prize, and activate it; they earn the accrued play revenue (withdrawRevenue) and the pool deposit is non-recoverable (pays out only as prizes). Players pay the GAS price to pull(); the contract draws a weighted item ON-CHAIN with Runtime.GetRandom and transfers the prize (GAS or NEO) atomically in the same tx. Odds are transparent: each item's draw probability is its weight share. Custody: player prepays via memo 'miniapp-gasbox:play'; an aborted pull leaves reusable play credit (no withdraw for play credit). Who-pays-whom: player→creator (revenue) and pool→player (prize).
apps.intended_workflow: Player: browse market → select a machine → review pull cost + odds coverage + per-item drop rates + prize-pool readiness checklist → Pull (prepay+pull in one settled tx) → on-chain prize transferred + result overlay. Creator: open Studio → name + price + prize asset + weighted items (live derived rarity tiers) → publish (createMachine → addItem ×N → fund pool to cover max prize → setActive) → later top up pool, toggle active, withdraw revenue. Money lifecycle: pool funded by creator (non-recoverable), revenue accrues per play and is withdrawable by the creator, prizes paid from pool to players.

gaps.title: Catalog manifest promises NFT and points prizes the contract cannot pay
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description: 'chances to win NEO, rare NFTs, or points' and tags ['gacha','blind-box','nft',…]. The deployed MiniAppGasBox only pays NEP-17 fungibles — prizeAsset is GAS or NEO (useGasBox.ts:93, assetSymbolFromHash :150-156, PRIZE_ASSET_OPTIONS ['GAS','NEO'] PlayArea.tsx:46); there is no NEP-11/NFT or 'points' prize path. The in-app copy is correct (docDescription 'draws a weighted item on-chain and transfers the prize') but the store listing over-promises prize types the product can't deliver.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: change the neo-manifest.json description/tags to the real prize set ('win NEO or GAS from on-chain prize pools with provably-fair weighted draws') and drop the 'nft' tag, so a newcomer's expectation matches the payable assets.

gaps.title: Player prepaid play-credit has no exit and the chip does not say so
gaps.evidence: If a pull is aborted after prepay, playCreditOf(player) holds GAS that is only re-consumed by the next pull — the contract exposes no play-credit withdraw (ABI has only withdrawRevenue for creators). The chip copy reads 'Prepaid credit … Your next pull uses it automatically' (locale gasboxPlayCreditHint:96-99), which is honest about auto-reuse but never warns the GAS cannot be withdrawn (unlike fogplay/tarot which do have withdraw).
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: append to gasboxPlayCreditHint that the credit is spendable on a future pull only and cannot be withdrawn to the wallet, so the player understands the credit is not refundable before relying on it.

apps.business_model: A random-GAS reward-distribution tool with two roles. (1) Campaign owner/creator: funds a pool that pays each recipient a RANDOM slice within a configured range (default 1-50 GAS) across N claim slots, distributed either on-chain (createRangeGasPool/claimRangeGasPool on PlatformSocial RangePool, testnet 0xfa1b7240… / mainnet 0x5f371cc5…) or via single-use claim keys redeemed through a backend (/api/onegate-vault/claim) that the server pays from a payout wallet. The creator recovers unclaimed GAS via refundRangeGasPool after expiry and recovers interrupted-create deposits via withdrawGasCredit. (2) Recipient: scans a OneGate QR carrying a one-time claim key and receives a server-decided random 1-50 GAS reward (frontend never decides the amount). Who-pays-whom: creator/server pool → recipients; one claim per address per pool.
apps.intended_workflow: Recipient path (QR launch): open the OneGate QR (key prefilled) → see the 1-50 GAS reward range + 'one claim per address' guard → Claim Reward → wallet/submit/confirm/paid progress → congratulations with amount + luck percentile + txid. Creator path (direct open): Create reward pool (total/min/max/slots/expiry, validated so total covers min×slots and ≤ max×slots) → distribute claim keys/QRs → inspect/top-up the pool → after expiry Recover remaining GAS (refund) → Check/Withdraw recoverable GAS credit from an interrupted create.

gaps.title: Default (non-QR) experience is an undescribed creator workspace; the catalog only describes the recipient claim
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description + operation_panel describe ONLY the recipient: 'Claim a server-backed 1-50 GAS random reward by scanning a OneGate QR…' with a single 'Claim Reward' operation. But when opened directly (no claimKey launch param) PlayArea renders the full creator workspace — Create reward pool, Pool controls (inspect/top-up/refund), and recoverable GAS credit (PlayArea.tsx:465-630). A first-time user who opens the app from the catalog lands on a campaign-builder they were never told about, with no explanation of who it is for or that it powers the QR rewards described in the listing.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add a short role-orienting header to the creator workspace ('Campaign owner? Fund a random-GAS reward pool here, then share OneGate QR claim links') and expand the neo-manifest.json description to name both roles (recipient claims via QR; campaign owners create/fund/recover pools), so the dual value-prop is legible before entry.

gaps.title: Two different reward engines (on-chain pool vs server-paid claim key) are conflated under one product with no explanation of which applies
gaps.evidence: createPool/claimPool(poolId) invoke the on-chain contract (useGasLuckyPool.ts createRangeGasPool :310, claimRangeGasPool :763), while claim-by-key goes through claimKeyThroughBackend → /api/onegate-vault/claim where the SERVER picks the amount and pays (:556-645). The creator workspace builds an on-chain pool, but the recipient flow the manifest advertises is server-backed; nothing tells a creator that the claim keys are redeemed off-chain by a backend, not against the pool they funded. The 'Server guarded' vs on-chain pool distinction is invisible.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: in the creator workspace, label the two distribution paths explicitly — 'On-chain pool (recipients call claimRangeGasPool)' vs 'OneGate claim keys (paid by the reward server)' — and in the docs/how-it-works clarify that QR claim keys are redeemed via the backend payout wallet, so creators and recipients share one accurate mental model of where the GAS comes from.

gaps.title: Recipient cannot verify the on-chain truth of a server-paid random reward before claiming
gaps.evidence: The recipient sees only the 1-50 GAS range and 'Server guarded' (locale rewardRangeDefault:78, contractGuarded:209); the actual amount is chosen by the backend and only revealed post-payout (claimCongratsBody, luckPercentLabel). docSafetyModel explains the server validates everything, but the recipient has no surfaced way to confirm the payout tx on-chain until after claiming, and the randomness is server-side (not Runtime.GetRandom), so it is trust-the-server by design.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: after a paid claim, surface a 'View on explorer' link for lastTxid in the recipient success card (the txid is already captured) so the recipient can independently verify the GAS transfer; optionally state up-front that the reward amount is decided and paid by the campaign's reward server.

apps.business_model: A FOMO/tontine all-pay pot game (winner-take-all). The user buys keys with GAS at a rising bonding-curve price (base 0.1 GAS/key, +0.1% per key already sold). Each purchase adds its full cost to a single growing prize pot and extends a live countdown (+30s/key, capped 24h) and makes the buyer the current 'last buyer'. The deployed standalone contract MiniAppLastSurvivor (testnet 0xe2385169… / mainnet 0x8e1e432e…) pays the recorded last buyer the ENTIRE pot atomically when settle() runs after the timer hits zero — permissionless, anyone can settle, no platform fee. Risk/custody: a key purchase is a non-refundable contribution to the pot; if someone outbids you before the clock expires you forfeit your entire spend; only the final last-buyer wins everything. Aborted-buy deposits are reclaimable via withdraw(account).
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → view round #, pot, danger meter/countdown, current leader → pick a key count → see the estimated (rising) cost → Buy Keys (deposit memo'd GAS then buyKeys() — resets your last-buyer status and extends the clock) → watch the danger meter; if the timer reaches zero you (as last buyer) win → anyone clicks Settle Round to pay the last buyer the whole pot and open the next round. Money lifecycle: key cost → pot (non-refundable contribution); winner takes the entire pot on settle; a deposit whose buy didn't complete is reusable or withdrawable.

gaps.title: 'Share %' metric can be misread as a proportional claim on the pot in a winner-take-all game
gaps.evidence: The participation bar shows 'Share' = userKeys/totalKeys as a percent (PlayArea.tsx:309-316, userSharePercent useLastSurvivor.ts:274-278). In a winner-take-all pot this share confers NO payout entitlement — only the single last buyer wins. A newcomer used to pooled/raffle games may read a 30% share as '30% of the pot' rather than 'I hold 30% of keys but win nothing unless I'm last'.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: relabel or annotate the Share metric to clarify it is participation only ('your key share — does not entitle you to the pot; only the last buyer wins'), reinforcing the winner-take-all model already stated in the rules.

gaps.title: The downside (a key purchase is a non-refundable contribution you lose if outbid) is implicit
gaps.evidence: Copy emphasizes the upside — subtitle 'Last buyer wins the entire prize pool', ruleWinDesc 'last buyer wins the entire pot on-chain — no platform fee' (locale:9, :147). The symmetric risk — that your key cost goes into the pot and is forfeited (won by someone else) if you are not the last buyer — is never stated as a risk before buying; the only 'recovery' copy (prepaidCreditHint) is for an aborted buy, which a user could conflate with getting their contribution back.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add a one-line risk note near the Buy Keys action ('Key purchases are non-refundable and added to the pot — if another player buys after you, you forfeit your spend; only the final last buyer wins'), so the loss case is as legible as the win case.

apps.business_model: A paid on-chain divination/entertainment app. The user pays a fixed 0.1 GAS draw fee; the deployed standalone contract MiniAppTarot (testnet/mainnet 0xb680225a…) draws three DISTINCT cards from a 78-card deck ON-CHAIN with Runtime.GetRandom in the same transaction and stores the reading, emitting ReadingDrawn(readingId,player,card0,card1,card2). There is no payout — the value is a provably-random, permanently on-chain Past/Present/Future spread the user can audit and replay (getReading). Who-pays-whom: the 0.1 GAS fee accrues to the contract as revenue, withdrawable by the owner (withdrawRevenue). Custody: fee prepaid via memo 'miniapp-tarot:draw'; an aborted draw leaves reusable credit that is withdrawable via withdraw(account). The typed question is kept on-device only, not on-chain.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → type a question (kept on-device, ≤200 chars) → see the 0.1 GAS draw fee + contract route (transfer → draw()) → Draw 3 Cards (deposit fee then draw() in one settled tx, cards from the ReadingDrawn event) → tap each card to reveal Past/Present/Future → read summary + Copy reading → Draw Again. Verification: fee shown in wallet before approval, cards drawn on-chain via Runtime.GetRandom, result auditable from the ReadingDrawn event. Exit: unused prepaid draw-credit from an aborted draw is reused or withdrawn back to the wallet.

apps.business_model: An all-pay, winner-takes-all seasonal GAS-burning competition (manifest category 'games'). User = anyone wanting to gamble/compete for a pot. Economic model (MiniAppBurnLeague 0xdd3bf2ff…): each player deposits GAS (memo, OnNEP17Payment credits) then burn(player,amount) adds it to the season's rewardPool and to userBurned; O(1) topBurner tracking. There is NO house fee — the entire pool is the prize. When the season clock (seasonDuration/seasonEnd) elapses, settle() pays the WHOLE pool to the single top burner; every other player forfeits their burn entirely. minBurn/maxBurn bound entries; withdraw(account) refunds unused prepaid credit from a deposit whose burn didn't complete. Permissionless settle. Pure zero-sum redistribution among burners.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) See season phase (dormant→active countdown→ended). 2) Enter a burn amount within min/max, preview projected season total + projected rank + current prize pool. 3) Deposit GAS then burn → climbs leaderboard. 4) During the season, top up to defend rank; watch countdown + current leader. 5) At expiry, anyone clicks Settle → whole pool pays the top burner; season rolls to next (dormant). 6) Loser money lifecycle: a burn that didn't complete leaves reusable prepaid credit, withdrawable to wallet. Money in = deposit; money out = pool to winner at settle, or credit-withdraw for stranded deposits.

gaps.title: Min/max burn bounds are hardcoded in the UI instead of read from the contract
gaps.evidence: apps/burn-league/src/PlayArea.tsx:35-36 define MIN_BURN=1, MAX_BURN=1000 as literals and useBurnLeague.ts:77-83 mirror them as constants, even though the deployed contract exposes minBurn()/maxBurn() (confirmed live on 0xdd3bf2ff…). If the contract bounds ever differ from the literals, the UI would validate against wrong limits and the burnRange copy (locale burnRange) would mislead.
gaps.fix: Bind the min/max inputs and the burnRange/burnRangeError copy to the already-available on-chain minBurn()/maxBurn() reads (surface them through the composable's state) and fall back to the literals only when the read is unavailable.

apps.business_model: A claim-first social GAS gifting app (manifest category 'social', featured). Two roles: recipient (primary) and creator (secondary). Economic model (MiniAppRedEnvelope 0x363c5de9…): a creator deposits GAS then createEnvelope(creator,totalAmount,packetCount,durationSeconds) splits the pool into packetCount random packets; each claim(envelopeId,claimer) draws ONE random packet and pays GAS to the claimer atomically in the same tx (WeChat lucky-money double-average split). No fee — the full pool is distributed to claimers. After expiry the creator reclaim()s unclaimed remainder; over/failed deposits sit as prepaid credit withdrawable via withdraw(). Distribution links shared via OneGate QR (envelope id prefills the claim).
apps.intended_workflow: Recipient path (primary): scan a OneGate QR / paste an envelope id / pick an active envelope → review the wallet request → claim → receive a random GAS share → celebration overlay + recent-claims update. Creator path (secondary): set total GAS + packet count + expiry → deposit-then-create → copy the shareable claim link → recipients claim random shares. Exit/recovery: after expiry the creator reclaims the unclaimed remainder; any stranded prepaid credit is withdrawable. Money in = creator deposit; money out = random packets to claimers, reclaim of remainder, or credit-withdraw.

gaps.title: Create summary frames packets as a fixed 'Average packet' instead of a random draw
gaps.evidence: apps/red-envelope/src/PlayArea.tsx:307-311 shows the create preview as 'Average packet' = perPacketGas (total/count). The contract pays each claimer a RANDOM share (double-average split), so a sender could read the preview as 'each recipient gets this exact amount'. The random nature is only stated in the claim-side safetyPanelCopy and createReadyDesc, not next to the create-preview number itself.
gaps.fix: Relabel/annotate the create-preview figure (perPacketLabel) to make randomness explicit at the point of creation, e.g. add a one-line caption under the 'Average packet' value reusing the existing createReadyDesc ('Each recipient draws a random share of the pool') so the average isn't mistaken for a guaranteed per-packet amount.

gaps.title: Large stale locale block for an NFT/NEO-gated model the contract does not implement
gaps.evidence: apps/red-envelope/src/locale/messages.ts carries an entire 'NFT pass-along' + 'dual-type envelope system' + NEO-eligibility vocabulary (myEnvelopes/transferEnvelope/mint/auto-burn, typeSpreading/typeLucky, neoRequirement/minNeoPlaceholder/holdingDays/eligible, flowBannerSpreading 'Mint NFT → Pass Along → Auto-burn'). The deployed ABI has no NFT/transfer/NEO-gate methods (only createEnvelope/claim/reclaim/withdraw) and the rendered PlayArea uses none of these keys — they are dead. Risk is future maintainers (or any leaked rendering) reintroducing a mental model the chain can't honor.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only cleanup: delete the unused NFT/dual-type/NEO-eligibility locale keys so the copy surface matches the claim-first contract model and cannot accidentally be wired to a non-existent feature.

apps.business_model: A two-party, matched-stake social commitment pact (manifest category 'social'). Users = two people who want a financial commitment device for a relationship/agreement. Economic model (MiniAppBreakupPact 0xf6769c08…): createPact(party1,party2,stake,durationSeconds) — party1 deposits a stake; party2 signPact deposits a MATCHING stake; both are escrowed. If either party breakPact()s, the breaker forfeits their stake and the other party receives BOTH stakes (loss-aversion incentive to honor). If the term elapses with no break, settlePact() (permissionless) refunds both stakes in full. While still pending (party2 never signed), party1 can cancel and reclaim. No house fee. Title/terms are off-chain (creator's device); only stake + duration + parties are on-chain. Stranded deposits recoverable via withdraw().
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Creator drafts a pact: partner address, matched stake, duration (≥30d), title+terms (off-chain) → deposit-then-create → status 'pending'. 2) Named partner reviews (warned terms are off-chain, verify together) and signPact with a matching stake → status 'active'. 3a) Either party breakPact → status 'broken', breaker forfeits, other side gets both stakes. 3b) Term elapses honored → anyone settlePact → status 'ended', both refunded. 3c) Pending & unsigned → creator cancel → status 'cancelled', stake reclaimed. Recovery: a stake deposited without completing create/sign sits as reusable credit, recoverable via withdraw. Money in = both stakes; money out = forfeit-to-partner, dual refund, cancel reclaim, or credit recovery.

gaps.title: Matched-stake / forfeit economics explainer disappears once the user has any pact
gaps.evidence: apps/breakup-contract/src/PlayArea.tsx:234 gates the How-it-works card (howItWorksStake/Break/Settle copy that explains 'each locks a matching stake; break = forfeit to partner; honor = both refunded') behind `!hasContracts && !lastSubmittedTitle && !serviceNotice`. A returning user creating a SECOND pact (the highest-stakes money action) no longer sees the forfeit/refund rules near the create form; the create form itself only shows contractDescription, which omits the matched-stake and forfeit consequences.
gaps.fix: Keep a concise economics line near the create CTA regardless of hasContracts — e.g. always render the existing clause1 locale string ('each locks a matching GAS stake. Break it and your stake goes to your partner; honor it to expiry and both stakes are refunded') as a hint under the stake input, or stop gating the How-it-works card on hasContracts.

apps.business_model: An on-chain tip jar / appreciation app for open-source developers (manifest category 'social'). Two roles: tippers (supporters) and registered developers (recipients). Economic model (MiniAppTipJar 0x6fdcf2ff…): a developer registerDeveloper(wallet,name,role) → gets a devId. A tipper deposits GAS (memo, OnNEP17Payment credits their tipper balance) then tip(tipper,devId,amount,anonymous) moves the amount from their credit to that developer's CLAIMABLE balance held by the contract (bumps lifetime totals, emits Tipped). The developer later withdrawTips(devId) to pull the accrued balance to their wallet. No platform fee — 100% of the amount is creditable to the dev. Unused tipper credit (over/failed deposit) is reclaimable via withdraw(). It is a custodial accrue-then-claim ledger, NOT a direct peer-to-peer transfer.
apps.intended_workflow: Tipper: connect wallet → pick a listed developer (name/role) or enter a registered devId → enter amount, choose anonymous or named → deposit-then-tip → amount accrues to the dev's claimable balance + appears in the on-chain ledger. Developer: register (name/role) → see 'Claimable Tips' balance accumulate as supporters tip → withdrawTips to move GAS to wallet. Recovery: a deposit whose tip step failed sits as reusable tipper credit, withdrawable. Money in = tipper deposit; money out = developer withdrawTips (delayed/pull), or tipper credit-withdraw.

gaps.title: Copy claims tips go 'directly to the developer's wallet' — but the model is custodial accrue-then-withdraw
gaps.evidence: Locale (apps/dev-tipping/src/locale/messages.ts) states feature1Desc '100% of your tip goes directly to the developer's wallet', step4 'Confirm transaction - tips go directly to developer', and docDescription 'sends GAS directly to developer wallets'. The contract (MiniAppTipJar.cs:23-31, confirmed live) does the opposite: tip() moves the amount into the developer's CLAIMABLE balance held in the contract; the developer must call withdrawTips() to receive GAS. The tipper isn't economically shortchanged (no fee), but the mechanism — and especially the implication of instant delivery — is wrong; a developer who is told tips arrive 'directly' may never know they must withdraw, and a tipper has no signal the dev hasn't yet been paid.
gaps.fix: Reword feature1Desc/step4/docDescription to the accrue-then-claim truth, e.g. '100% of your tip (no platform fee) accrues to the developer's on-chain balance, which they withdraw to their wallet.' This is frontend-only locale copy.

gaps.title: Developer Zone does not explain that tips accrue here and must be withdrawn
gaps.evidence: apps/dev-tipping/src/components/DeveloperPanel.tsx:54-73 shows a 'Claimable Tips' figure + Withdraw button but no explanatory copy that incoming tips land here (not in the wallet) and require a withdraw to realize. A newly-registered developer seeing 0 has no cue that future tips will sit in this balance, and registerHint only says 'Register your wallet to receive tips'.

apps.business_model: A community public-goods grants platform using quadratic (CLR) matching (manifest category 'finance'). Roles: round operator/admin (funds the matching pool), project owners (apply for funding), donors (contribute small amounts). Economic model (MiniAppQuadraticFunding 0xe2fba2a73c…, kernel-style with admin/oracle/gateway): createRound(creator,asset,matchingPool,start,end,…) locks a GAS matching pool; registerProject lists projects; contribute(contributor,roundId,projectId,amount,memo) records donor contributions per project (totalContributed + unique contributorCount = the 'donor signal'). The quadratic property: matching ∝ breadth of unique donors, so many small donations beat one whale. Matching is computed off-chain (admin finalizeRound(operator,roundId,projectIds,matchedAmounts), gated by admin() and round-end); project owners claimProject to receive contributions+match; creators claimUnusedMatching for dust; cancelRound refunds the pool if no contributions before start. No per-tx fee. Direct contributions go to projects; the pool amplifies them.
apps.intended_workflow: Operator: create a round (matching pool, schedule). Project owners: register a project (name/mission/link) into the round. Donors: during the active window, contribute GAS to specific projects (each unique donor strengthens that project's quadratic weight). At round end, admin computes matches off-chain (UI offers a suggested-match table from on-chain donor breadth × totals) and finalizeRound on-chain. Project owners claimProject (contributions + matched amount). Creator claimUnusedMatching for leftover pool dust. cancelRound refunds the matching deposit only before start with no contributions. Money in = matching pool + donor contributions; money out = project claims (contrib+match), creator unused-matching claim, or cancel refund.

gaps.title: Donor never sees the quadratic-amplification value prop at the moment of contributing
gaps.evidence: The entire reason a donor uses QF (a small donation gets amplified by the matching pool, and breadth of donors matters more than size) is never surfaced on the donor's path. The hero (apps/quadratic-funding/src/components/FundingHero.tsx:43-44) says only 'Fund public goods with matching power' / generic subtitle and the contribute tab (PlayArea.tsx:336-376) is a bare round/project/amount/memo form with hint qfContributionHint ('Contribution calls are signed against the selected round and project ID') — no preview of estimated matching, no 'why small/many donations matter'. The suggested-match computation (composables/quadraticMatch.ts) exists but is shown only in the admin RoundAdminPanel, not to donors.
gaps.fix: On the contribute tab, surface the matching effect for the selected project using the already-computed suggestedMatches/round pool data — e.g. show the project's current matched estimate and a line like 'Each unique donor increases this project's match; small donations from many people are amplified most.' Frontend-only, reusing existing reads.

gaps.title: UI does not disclose that the suggested match is an equal-split approximation, not exact CLR
gaps.evidence: composables/quadraticMatch.ts documents that, because the contract only exposes per-project aggregates (totalContributed, contributorCount) and not per-donor amounts, the suggested weight uses the equal-split estimate weight_i = n_i·T_i rather than the canonical (Σ√c_ij)². The admin sees 'Suggested match' (locale matchTableSuggested) presented as authoritative with no caveat that it is an approximation an operator should sanity-check before finalizing real funds.
gaps.fix: Add a short caveat near the suggested-match table / finalizeSuggested button (extend the existing finalizeHint copy) noting the suggestion is an on-chain-data approximation of quadratic matching that the operator can override. Frontend-only copy.

apps.business_model: A free (zero-fee) on-chain conditional escrow for B2B/freelance delivery payments. The user is a CREATOR (buyer/payer) who locks NEO or GAS for a single named project and splits it into 1-12 milestones; the BENEFICIARY (contractor/vendor) is paid per milestone. Economic model verified against MiniAppMilestoneEscrow ABI: createEscrow/approveMilestone/claimMilestone/cancelEscrow with NO platform fee anywhere in the ABI (no fee field, releases are the full milestone amount), so the value prop is trust-minimized staged release, not a marketplace that takes a cut. Custody: funds sit in the contract; the creator gates release by approving each milestone, the beneficiary pulls the approved tranche, and the creator can cancel to refund all UNAPPROVED funds (EscrowCancelled carries refundAmount). The deposit is a two-step prepay (NEP-17 transfer with memo 'miniapp-milestone-escrow:fund', then createEscrow consumes the credit).
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Creator opens Create, names the escrow, enters a beneficiary N3 address, picks NEO or GAS, adds 1-12 milestone amounts (live sum shown, must equal the deposit). 2) Creator signs the deposit transfer, then signs createEscrow (two wallet prompts); funds are now locked on-chain. 3) As deliverables are accepted, the creator approves each milestone (MilestoneApproved). 4) The beneficiary claims each approved tranche to their wallet (MilestoneClaimed); unapproved funds stay locked. 5) Exit/recovery: the creator can cancelEscrow at any time to reclaim all not-yet-approved funds; if the deposit lands but createEscrow fails, the prepaid credit is held under the creator and reused on retry. Lifecycle states: active -> completed (all milestones claimed) or cancelled (refund).

gaps.title: Two-signature deposit-then-create flow is not disclosed before the creator commits
gaps.evidence: useMilestoneEscrow.ts createEscrow() fires a NEP-17 transfer (PAYMENT_MEMO 'miniapp-milestone-escrow:fund') and waits for confirmation, THEN invokes createEscrow — two distinct wallet signatures (composable lines ~421-486). The create form in PlayArea.tsx (lines 162-229) shows no notice of this; the sibling neo-pay app explicitly renders t('twoStepSignNotice') for the identical pattern. A first-timer expects one signature and may abandon after the first prompt, leaving prepaid credit on the contract.
gaps.fix: Add a one-line disclosure under the Submit button (e.g. reuse the depositPrepaidNoEscrow framing or add a new key) stating that creating an escrow needs two wallet signatures — first the {asset} deposit, then the escrow setup — mirroring neo-pay's twoStepSignNotice.

gaps.title: Free / no-fee nature of the escrow is never stated as a value prop
gaps.evidence: The contract ABI has no fee field and releases the full milestone amount (no deduction in MiniAppMilestoneEscrow.Methods.cs). Yet no copy tells the user the service is free — the hero (MilestoneHero.tsx) and docDescription describe mechanics but not the economic model. For an escrow product, 'who pays the platform and how much' is a primary trust/decision factor; its absence leaves users guessing whether a cut is taken.
gaps.fix: Add a short hero/doc line such as 'No platform fee — beneficiaries receive the full milestone amount; you only pay network gas.' Frontend copy only.

gaps.title: Beneficiary cannot tell that payout depends on creator approval before engaging
gaps.evidence: The role model is creator-approves / beneficiary-claims (claimMilestone requires the milestone be approved first; useMilestoneEscrow gates the claim button on milestoneApproved). EscrowBody/EscrowList surface per-milestone pills (Pending/Approved/Claimed) but no upfront statement that a beneficiary is dependent on the creator unilaterally approving — a beneficiary could mistake the locked total for guaranteed funds.
gaps.fix: On beneficiary-side cards (or the 'For you' section header) add a short note: 'Funds release only after the creator approves each milestone.' Copy/affordance only over existing reads.

apps.business_model: A shared on-chain custody vault (M-of-N multisig treasury) for teams/DAOs/co-owned funds. Users are 2-16 SIGNERS who jointly control GAS/NEO; no single key can move funds. Verified against MiniAppMultisig ABI: createVault(signers, threshold) -> vaultId; deposits credited via OnNEP17Payment using vaultId as transfer data; createRequest proposes a spend; approve() collects signatures; the contract auto-executes the transfer when the approval threshold is met (RequestExecuted). No fee in the ABI — the value is custody safety and threshold enforcement, not revenue. v2 twist verified on-chain: a threshold approval that finds the vault underfunded auto-cancels the request (RequestUnfunded event). Custody is fully on-chain; any signer can cancel a pending request.
apps.intended_workflow: Step 1 create a vault from 2-16 signer addresses + a threshold (e.g. 2-of-3). Step 2 deposit GAS/NEO into the vault (NEP-17 transfer carrying the vaultId; credits the vault balance). Step 3 a signer proposes a spend (recipient, asset, amount, memo) and shares the request ID. Step 4 each listed signer loads the request and approves; when approvals reach the threshold the contract releases the funds in the same call. Lifecycle: pending -> executed (threshold met) / cancelled (any signer cancels, or auto-cancelled if the vault is underfunded at the moment of the threshold approval). Recovery: deposited funds remain in the vault and can be re-proposed; an underfunded auto-cancel prompts re-deposit then re-propose.

gaps.title: Vault funds are pooled, not earmarked per request — multiple pending requests can race for the same balance
gaps.evidence: BalanceKey is per (vault, asset) and proposing a request does NOT escrow/earmark funds; only the threshold approval debits the balance, and if short it auto-cancels (RequestUnfunded, confirmed by t('multisigUnfundedNotice') and the on-chain event). The pre-flight spendExceedsBalance check (PlayArea.tsx lines 129-144) compares against the whole vault balance, so two pending requests can each look fundable yet collide. The UI explains the post-hoc auto-cancel but not that pending proposals don't reserve funds.
gaps.fix: Add a brief note near the propose form or request status (e.g. 'Vault balance is shared across all pending requests — funds aren't reserved until a request reaches its threshold') so signers understand why an approved request can still auto-cancel. Copy only.

apps.business_model: A no-liquidation, no-interest collateralized line: the user locks whole NEO as collateral and instantly borrows GAS from an owner-funded GAS pool at a chosen LTV tier (20%/30%/40%), paying a one-time 0.5% origination fee. Verified against MiniAppSelfLoan ABI/source: borrow(borrower, tier) sets debt = collateralValue x ltvBps/10000 (collateralValue = NEO x owner-set neoPrice), disburses gross - fee, fee stays in the pool as the owner's revenue; repay() applies prepaid GAS credit, caps at debt, refunds excess, and on full repayment releases the NEO. The contract has NO liquidation, NO interest, and NO time lock (repay is allowed immediately). The owner sets neoPrice (static 'council price', not an oracle) and funds/withdraws the GAS pool (withdrawPool) — so the owner is the lender earning the origination fee and bearing NEO-price risk. Reclaim paths (withdraw/withdrawRepayCredit) recover stranded deposit-then-act credits.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet; the app reads neoPrice, pool liquidity, LTV tiers and the 0.5% fee. 2) Enter whole-NEO collateral, pick an LTV tier; the form previews the net GAS you'll receive (gross minus fee), the rate (1 NEO = X GAS), and pool availability. 3) Borrow = two signed steps: deposit NEO (memo 'selfloan:collateral'), then borrow(tier) which locks ALL credited NEO, sets the debt, and disburses net GAS. 4) Manage: add collateral (another NEO deposit) or repay (deposit GAS with memo 'selfloan:repay' then repay()); full repayment closes the loan and returns the NEO. 5) Recovery: if a deposit lands but the act fails, reclaim collateral/repay credit. One active loan per address. No liquidation: the health-factor gauge is purely informational.

gaps.title: UI claims the locked collateral 'votes' via ProfitAnchor — the contract has no voting at all
gaps.evidence: MiniAppSelfLoan has zero vote/ProfitAnchor/candidate/Vote methods (grep of contracts/MiniAppSelfLoan/*.cs returns no voting; collateral NEO just sits in contract custody and is returned on repay). Yet the app surfaces a 'ProfitAnchor Vote Route — Collateral vote signal — Operator-selected council candidate' footnote (PlayArea.tsx lines 512-519), a live sidebar stat (manifest.ts line 44 profitAnchorStatus/profitAnchorValue), and a docs feature (manifest.ts line 60). The manifest description also states collateral 'follows ProfitAnchor's selected manual route.' This tells the user their collateral earns/participates in council voting when on-chain it does nothing of the sort — a material misrepresentation of what happens to locked funds.
gaps.fix: Remove or rewrite the ProfitAnchor claims to match reality: either drop the vote-route footnote, sidebar stat (manifest profitAnchorStatus row), and docs feature, or reword to 'Collateral is held in SelfLoan custody and returned on repayment (no third-party voting).' Frontend/manifest copy only; contracts are frozen.

gaps.title: Docs state a 24-hour minimum lock and 'Repay anytime after 24 hours' that the contract does not enforce
gaps.evidence: MiniAppSelfLoan.cs Repay() has no timestamp/duration gate (only 'no active loan'/'no repay credit' asserts); the composable hard-codes minDurationHours: 0 (useSelfLoan.ts borrowTerms/positionTerms). But locale messages.ts ships note ('Collateral locks until repaid (min 24h)'), step4/feature2Desc ('Repay anytime after 24 hours to unlock your collateral'), and minDuration='Minimum duration' / hours='hours'. These render in the How-It-Works docs and mislead users into thinking funds are locked for 24h.
gaps.fix: Update the copy to 'Repay anytime to unlock your collateral — no minimum lock, no interest' and drop the min-duration phrasing. Locale-only.

gaps.title: The origination fee's destination and the static, owner-set price are not disclosed as risk
gaps.evidence: The 0.5% fee is previewed (PlayArea.tsx lines 416-421) but not that it is the lender/owner's revenue retained in the pool (MiniAppSelfLoan.cs Borrow: 'fee stays in the pool as revenue'). neoPrice is an owner-set static value (loadNeoPrice reads neoPrice(); contract comment 'NOT a live oracle, matching the app's static council price'), so the borrow size and the health-factor gauge depend on an admin-controlled price, not a market — a transparency point the UI labels only as 'Rate'.
gaps.fix: Add a short note near the Rate/fee rows: 'Rate is set by the operator (not a live market oracle); the 0.5% origination fee is retained by the lending pool.' Copy only over existing reads (neoPrice, feeBps).

apps.business_model: A token-streaming / vesting tool for payroll, subscriptions, allowances, and treasury releases. The user is a CREATOR who locks GAS or NEO and defines a per-day linear release schedule; the BENEFICIARY claims vested amounts over time. Verified against the MiniAppNeoPay ABI used by useNeoPayApp: createStream(creator, beneficiary, asset, total, rate, intervalSeconds, title, notes) after a prepay deposit (memo 'miniapp-neo-pay:fund'); claimStream(beneficiary, id) pulls vested funds; cancelStream(creator, id) returns unvested funds. No protocol fee — value is trustless time-based release and creator-side cancelability. Custody on-chain; NEO sub-1-per-day collapses to a single end-of-term cliff (deriveSchedule).
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Creator enters recipient, amount, duration (days), token; the form previews the derived per-day release (linear) or warns of a single-cliff release for sub-1-NEO/day, plus a two-signature notice. 2) Creator signs the deposit then createStream (funds lock, schedule starts immediately). 3) Beneficiary sees incoming streams with progress bar and a live 'Claimable' figure and claims when >0 (claim gated on positive claimable to avoid a reverting tx). 4) Creator can cancel an active stream to reclaim unvested funds (claim/cancel are role-separated into 'Your Created Streams' vs 'Streams You Receive'). Lifecycle: active -> completed (fully claimed) / cancelled (unvested refunded). Recovery: a deposit that lands without a created stream leaves reusable prepaid credit.

gaps.title: Created-stream cards omit the per-day release rate the creator just configured
gaps.evidence: StreamItem carries rateAmount/intervalDays (parseStreamDetails in useNeoPayApp.ts) and the create form previews releasePerDay, but the 'Your Created Streams' cards (PlayArea.tsx lines 471-541) show only total, recipient, duration and a streamed/total progress bar — not the release rate. The beneficiary side surfaces 'Claimable' but the creator never sees the ongoing release-per-day they committed to.
gaps.fix: Render the per-day release (rateAmount/interval, already parsed) on the created-stream cards, reusing the releasePerDayValue locale key. Frontend only over existing reads.

apps.business_model: A two-sided atomic-liquidity market. BORROWERS (power users with a deployed callback contract) take an uncollateralized GAS loan that must be repaid principal + 0.09% fee within the same transaction (requestLoan transfers GAS to the callback's onFlashLoan, then asserts the pool is repaid exactly principal+fee or the whole tx reverts). LIQUIDITY PROVIDERS deposit GAS into the pool and earn the fee — confirmed on testnet getFlashLoanConstants: providerFeeShare = 80 (LPs get 80% of fees, protocol 20%), feesBasisPoints = 9 (0.09%), minLoan 1 GAS, maxLoan 100,000 GAS, cooldown 300s, maxDailyLoans 10. Fees accrue to the pool and are pushed to providers via distributeFees(). Withdraw caps at the provider's tracked balance; getProviderStatsDetails exposes totalFeesEarned.
apps.intended_workflow: Borrower path: deploy a contract implementing onFlashLoan(borrower, amount, fee, loanId) that repays principal+fee in-transaction; enter amount + callback contract; the calculator shows fee (0.09%) and total repayment, plus min/max, cooldown, daily limit; sign requestLoan — it executes atomically (success/failed/pending status via getLoanDetails). LP path: deposit GAS to the pool (earns 80% of fees), monitor 'Your Liquidity' and 'Fees Earned', withdraw up to deposited at any time. Lookup any loan by ID; recent executions table shows history. Lifecycle: loan pending -> executed(success/failed); LP deposit -> withdraw.

gaps.title: LP fee economics understated — 80% provider share and the distributeFees step are not surfaced
gaps.evidence: On-chain getFlashLoanConstants returns providerFeeShare = 80 (LPs earn 80% of the 0.09% fee, protocol keeps 20%) and the contract has a distributeFees() method that pushes accrued fees to providers. The LP surface (PlayArea.tsx lines 409-466) only says t('liquidityInfo') 'earn a share of the 0.09% fee' and shows a 'Fees Earned' figure, but never states the 80% share or that fees show up only after distribution — so an LP cannot evaluate the actual yield or understand why 'Fees Earned' may lag pool activity.
gaps.fix: Surface providerFeeShare (already in getFlashLoanConstants/getPlatformStats — read it via contractStats) in the liquidity card, e.g. 'Liquidity providers earn 80% of each 0.09% loan fee (20% protocol).' Optionally add a note that fees are credited when distributeFees runs. Read + copy only.

gaps.title: First-timers without a callback contract have no usable path and the requirement is buried
gaps.evidence: Every loan requires a deployed contract implementing onFlashLoan (validateLoanRequest rejects a missing/invalid callbackContract). The locale has instructionMode/instructionNote ('Flash loans remain a power-user flow...') keys but they are NOT rendered in PlayArea.tsx; only a small inline callback note (lines 305-315) appears under the form. A non-developer sees a borrow form they can never complete, with no upfront 'this is a developer/power-user tool' framing or guidance toward the LP side (which they CAN use).
gaps.fix: Render the existing instructionMode/instructionNote copy as a prominent banner at the top of the request workspace, and point non-developers toward the Provide Liquidity card. Copy/layout only.

apps.business_model: A two-sided 'mercenary governance' market on a standalone on-chain contract (MiniAppGovMerc, ABI: stakeOf/totalStaked, bid/highestBid, settleEpoch, claimRewards, pendingRewards, reclaimBid, withdraw). TWO user roles: (1) STAKERS lock whole NEO (governance weight) by transferring NEO with memo 'govmerc:stake'; they earn revenue. (2) MERCENARIES bid GAS each epoch (memo 'govmerc:bid', first bid >= 1 GAS via minBid()) competing for the epoch 'router/winner' title. Economic model: the winning bidder's GAS is distributed PRO-RATA to NEO stakers (MasterChef accumulator); stakers claim it as GAS (claimRewards). Losing bidders pull-refund their bid (reclaimBid) and unused bid credit (withdraw). settleEpoch() is permissionless. The manifest/README frame it as a 'vote rental marketplace like Curve War' / 'voting power delegation', but the FROZEN contract has NO vote/delegate/governance-routing method — 'winning' only confers a title + pays stakers. So the real product is: stake NEO to earn an auctioned GAS yield; bid GAS to win an epoch title.
apps.intended_workflow: Staker path: connect wallet -> deposit NEO into the shared pool (transfer w/ memo) -> accrue GAS rewards pro-rata as epochs are settled -> claim rewards anytime -> withdraw NEO stake to exit (banks pending rewards first). Mercenary path: review current epoch + current highest bid + min bid -> place a GAS bid (first bid >= 1 GAS opens a fixed 5-min window) -> if window still open, raise; once the deadline passes bidding closes -> anyone calls settleEpoch() after the deadline: top bid wins, GAS paid to stakers, epoch advances -> losing bidders reclaim their bid from the settled epoch and withdraw unused credit. Money lifecycle: NEO custodied by contract (recoverable via withdrawStake); winning GAS leaves bidder -> stakers; losing GAS recoverable via reclaimBid/withdraw.

gaps.title: Hero/README promise 'governance delegation / vote rental' but nothing on-chain routes a vote
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description='Marketplace for governance voting power delegation'; README.md='vote rental marketplace like Curve War'; messages.ts flowInfluence='Route governance' / settleCopy='the top GAS bid wins and directs the pooled NEO influence'. But MiniAppGovMerc.manifest.json ABI has NO vote/delegate/setTarget method — settleEpoch only records settlementWinner(epoch) and pays the winning GAS to stakers. A newcomer is told they can rent/direct NEO votes; on-chain the winner gets only a title and the staked NEO never casts or delegates a vote.
gaps.fix: Reframe copy to the actual mechanism the contract enforces: 'Stake NEO to earn the GAS auction yield; bid GAS to win the epoch's influence title.' Replace 'directs the pooled influence' with what settlement actually does (records the winner, pays GAS to stakers). Add a one-line 'How influence is used' disclosure clarifying the winner title is recorded on-chain but vote execution is off-contract, so users don't expect an automatic on-chain delegation.

gaps.title: Staker yield economics (bid GAS -> stakers pro-rata) hidden before deposit
gaps.evidence: The single biggest reason to deposit NEO (you earn the auctioned GAS pro-rata) is only explained in the secondary 'Staker rewards' card (rewardsCopy) AFTER you scroll past deposit. The hero (MercHeroStats: totalPool/activeBids/currentEpoch) and the deposit action card (actionDepositHint='Add NEO voting power to the shared pool') never state that depositors receive GAS revenue. A first-time user sees 'deposit NEO for voting power' with no yield rationale.
gaps.fix: Surface the staker value-prop at the deposit point: add a line under depositNeo like 'NEO stakers split every epoch's winning GAS bid pro-rata' and show a hero stat for cumulative/last-epoch GAS distributed (derive from EpochSettled events / settlementAmount). This is frontend-only over existing reads.

gaps.title: Minimum bid (1 GAS) not shown until a bid fails
gaps.evidence: Contract enforces minBid()=1 GAS (useGovMerc MIN_BID=1; ABI minBid() is safe/readable). The bid action card (MercActionCards) only renders the 'First bid must be at least {amount}' error AFTER a failed submit via the minBid message; no minBid is displayed up front. grep confirms no minBid/minStake string in PlayArea.tsx or components/.
gaps.fix: Read minBid() (already in ABI/hook) and show it in the bid card as helper text ('Minimum first bid: 1 GAS') and as the input placeholder/min. Same for minStake() if non-zero. Frontend-only surfaced read.

gaps.title: Pool stat shows NEO weight but never the prize at stake (highest current bid)
gaps.evidence: MercHeroStats shows totalPool (NEO), activeBids count, currentEpoch — but not highestBid(currentEpoch), which is the GAS prize a mercenary must beat and the GAS stakers will receive this epoch. A bidder cannot see what bid they must outbid without scanning the leaderboard.
gaps.fix: Add a 'Current top bid' figure (highestBid(currentEpoch) ÷1e8, already read for the leaderboard) to the hero scoreboard or settle panel so both bidders (target to beat) and stakers (incoming yield) see the live prize.

gaps.title: Deposit/withdraw labeled 'voting power' though no vote is cast
gaps.evidence: messages.ts depositNeo/actionDepositHint and feature2Desc='Deposited NEO aggregates voting power on-chain' imply the NEO actively votes. The contract only tracks stake for reward-share weighting; it does not vote.
gaps.fix: Adjust copy from 'voting power' to 'stake weight / reward share' to match what the contract does with the NEO (weights the GAS payout split), avoiding the implication that the pool votes on Neo governance.

apps.business_model: An on-chain DAO/council voting front-end for a governance contract (testnet 0x4c61e557..., mainnet 0xc7e50e67...). User = a Neo council member (top-21 candidate). Value: council members create Text or Policy-change proposals, vote For/Against, and execute passed Policy proposals against Neo's native PolicyContract (FeePerByte, ExecFeeFactor, StoragePrice, MaxBlockSize, MaxTxPerBlock, MaxSystemFee). Eligibility is gated on-chain via isCandidate(address); non-candidates and disconnected wallets are read-only. Proposals from neo.community are mirrored read-only for context. No fees/payments — it is a pure governance-action tool. Lifecycle states: pending/active/passed/rejected/revoked/expired/executed, with finalize -> execute (policy) and creator revoke.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect a council wallet -> app verifies isCandidate -> browse Active proposals (with live quorum X/21 and For/Against split) -> open details -> vote For/Against (one vote, gated by hasVoted) -> when a proposal reaches its outcome the creator/member finalizes it -> for a passed POLICY proposal, Execute applies the PolicyContract change on-chain (distinct step) -> creator can Revoke their own still-active proposal -> History tab tracks resolved proposals. Mirror (neo.community) proposals are view-only with a clear note to vote through the native flow.

gaps.title: 'Voting Power' stat is a binary 1/0 candidate flag, not an explained weight
gaps.evidence: useGovernance.ts sets votingPower = eligible ? 1 : 0 (line ~569) and PlayArea renders it as a bare number in the stat strip labeled 'Voting Power'. A newcomer sees '1' or '0' with no indication it means 'are you 1 of the 21 council members'. The richer eligibility copy lives only in the access banner.
gaps.fix: Relabel the stat to 'Council Seat' showing 'Verified / Read-only', or render the votingPower number with a caption ('1 vote — council member'). Frontend-only; ties the stat to the top-21 candidate model already explained by notCandidate copy.

gaps.title: Quorum requirement (21) only legible on proposals that carry it; no global threshold context
gaps.evidence: Proposal cards show 'Quorum: {totalVotes}/{quorumRequired || "—"}'; when the contract returns 0/empty quorumRequired the user sees a dash with no idea what passing requires. The notCandidate copy reveals '21 council members' but the quorum bar never states the council size.
gaps.fix: When quorumRequired is unavailable, fall back to the known council size (21) as the denominator or add a 'Council of 21' caption near the quorum bar so the pass bar is legible. Frontend-only copy/fallback.

apps.business_model: Per the manifest (description='Preview NEO and GAS conversions with live pricefeed quotes, slippage context, and wallet-ready settlement notes', contracts:{}), this is a NEO<->GAS quote previewer, NOT a working DEX. It pulls live NEO/GAS prices from the Morpheus data feed, computes an exchange rate, slippage tolerance (0.5%) and minimum-received, and is WIRED to call swapTokenInForTokenOut on a router — but no router contract is deployed (routerAvailable = Boolean(chain.contractAddress) which is empty). So on every supported network the swap CTA is permanently disabled and settlement can never occur. The honest product is a price-quote / trade-planning console. Tags ('swap','dex','exchange') and the title 'Neo Swap' over-promise a working exchange.
apps.intended_workflow: Intended-as-built: connect wallet -> pick from/to (NEO/GAS) -> enter amount -> see live rate, slippage, min-received, and a route-status badge -> (if a router existed) submit swap and receive tokens. Actual deliverable: everything up to the quote works; the route badge reads 'Quote ready/Route unavailable' and a notice explains 'No on-chain swap router is deployed... on-chain settlement is not available', so the user can plan a trade but must execute it elsewhere. No funds move; no custody.

gaps.title: Primary CTA presents as the swap button despite never being actionable
