apps.business_model: A transparency dashboard + connected-wallet payout console (manifest category='tools', contracts:{}, operation_panel.submitDisbursement). User = anyone wanting to (a) watch public Neo founder/foundation wallet balances (hardcoded Da Hongfei + Erik Zhang address groups) read-only with live NEO/GAS/USD totals, and (b) sign a real NEP-17 transfer of NEO/GAS FROM THEIR OWN connected wallet to any recipient with a memo. There is NO treasury contract and no custody — the 'disbursement' is a plain self-funded transfer; the watched foundation wallets are strictly observational and unrelated to the recipient. Economic model: no fees, no pool; the app simply reads chain balances and relays a wallet-signed NEP-17 transfer.
apps.intended_workflow: Open app -> read public watched-wallet balances (Da Hongfei / Erik Zhang groups, with USD via price feed; em-dash on RPC/price failure) -> optionally refresh -> to make a payout: choose asset (GAS/NEO), amount, recipient (N...), memo -> preview the 'signing intent' (native contract, fixed-8 amount, recipient Hash160, your signer) -> connect wallet -> sign -> see txid receipt. Funds leave the connected wallet only; watched wallets never move. Exit: nothing custodied, so no recovery needed.

gaps.title: 'Treasury disbursement' framing implies spending the watched treasury, but funds come from your own wallet to an arbitrary recipient
gaps.evidence: Title 'Neo Treasury', disbursementTitle='Disbursement console', and the watchlist of foundation wallets sit directly above a 'Sign Disbursement' form. The recipient field is freeform ('N...') and the transfer is from the connected wallet (treasuryOperations builds a self-funded NEP-17 transfer). A newcomer can read this as 'disburse from the Neo treasury' when it is just 'send my own GAS/NEO to anyone'. disbursementBoundary copy does clarify, but it is one line under the heading.
gaps.fix: Make the source/destination unmistakable at the form: label the signer line 'From: your connected wallet' and add a short caption on the recipient field ('Any Neo address — paid from your wallet, not the watched treasury'). Visually separate the read-only watchlist section from the payout console with a 'Your wallet' header. Frontend-only copy/labels.

gaps.title: Recipient has no relationship to the watched wallets, but the watchlist offers no way to use a watched address as a payout target
gaps.evidence: The product juxtaposes 'watch these treasury wallets' with 'send a disbursement', yet the only natural connected workflow (pay one of the watched treasury wallets) requires manual copy-paste of the address — wallet rows show compactAddress only. The two halves of the app never connect.
gaps.fix: Add a 'Use as recipient' action on each watched wallet row that fills the recipient field, making the dashboard->payout flow coherent (and reinforcing that you are paying TO the treasury, not from it). Frontend-only; the addresses are already in the watch list.

apps.business_model: An onboarding faucet + community pay-it-forward tool (manifest category='tools', tags gas/sponsor/onboarding/free). User = a new, low-balance Neo wallet (< 0.1 GAS) who needs GAS to pay tx fees. Value: request up to 0.1 GAS/day FREE. Economic model: the free GAS is fronted by a platform paymaster (off-chain HTTP API, VITE_PLATFORM_API) with a per-day quota; eligibility = balance < 0.1 GAS AND quota remaining. The pool is replenished by community DONATIONS — users with funds donate GAS to a hardcoded pool wallet (NhWxcoEc9qtmnjsTLF1fVF6myJ5MZZhSMK), or directly Send GAS to another address. Donate/Send are pure on-chain GAS transfers (work independently of the API); the sponsorship request depends entirely on the platform API, which is optional and currently unconfigured/down (per memory), so the faucet degrades to an honest 'unavailable' notice.
apps.intended_workflow: New user: connect wallet -> app checks eligibility (balance < 0.1 GAS) and remaining daily quota via the platform API -> request up to remaining quota -> platform sponsors the GAS (request_id receipt) -> use it for fees -> quota resets daily UTC. Funded user (pay-it-forward, gated behind chainGasBalance>0): Donate GAS to the sponsor pool wallet, or Send GAS to a specific address to help someone. Money: faucet GAS comes from the platform paymaster/pool; donations flow user -> pool; sends flow user -> recipient. When the API is down, request is disabled with a notice and only donate/send remain.

gaps.title: The funding loop (donations replenish the pool that sponsors new users) is never stated, breaking the value-prop of donating
gaps.evidence: handleDonate transfers GAS to the hardcoded SPONSOR_POOL_ADDRESS, and step4 says 'Once you have enough GAS, help others!'. But the donate copy (donateSubtitle='Help new users get started', payForwardLead) never tells the donor that the pool they fund is the SAME pool that sponsors the faucet requests — the economic circle (donate -> pool -> sponsored requests) is invisible. The pool address itself is also never shown, so a donor can't verify where funds go.
gaps.fix: Add copy on the Donate form making the loop explicit ('Donations top up the sponsorship pool that funds new-user GAS requests') and surface/short-display the pool address for verifiability. Frontend-only over the existing poolAddress constant.

gaps.title: Send (arbitrary GAS transfer) is conflated with the sponsorship/donation mission
gaps.evidence: The 'Send GAS' form is a generic wallet transfer to any address (handleSend -> NEP-17 transfer), framed as sendSubtitle='Help someone with low GAS balance'. It does not interact with the sponsor pool, eligibility, or quota at all — it is a plain send dressed as part of the sponsorship product, which can confuse a user about whether it counts toward 'sponsoring'.
gaps.fix: Clarify in copy that Send is a direct peer transfer (not pool-mediated and not tracked by the faucet), e.g. 'Send GAS directly to a friend — this does not go through the sponsorship pool.' Frontend-only copy.

gaps.title: When the sponsorship API is down, the headline still promises 'Get free GAS' with no path
gaps.evidence: Hero subtitle='Get free GAS for transactions' and docDescription promise the faucet, but per memory VITE_PLATFORM_API is unset so serviceAvailable can be false; the request card then shows the unavailable notice while the eligibility gauge reads 'Unavailable'. A new low-balance user — the exact target — arrives for free GAS and finds only donate/send (which they cannot use with a near-zero balance).
gaps.fix: When serviceAvailable is false, adapt the hero/CTA to set expectations ('Free GAS faucet is temporarily offline — check back, or ask a funded wallet to Send you GAS') instead of leading with 'Get free GAS'. Frontend-only over the existing serviceAvailable signal.

apps.business_model: A developer/power-user tool for Neo Account Abstraction. The user is someone provisioning or auditing a Neo Abstract Account 'shell' on the shared UnifiedSmartWalletV3 AA core (mainnet 0x0268a387..., domain core.smartwallet.neo). Value: (1) inspect an existing account's verifier/hook/backup-owner/escape-timelock/escape-status before trusting it; (2) register a NEW account shell with an explicit social-recovery posture (a backup owner who can recover after an escape timelock of 7-90 days). Economic model: no fee or reward — the only cost is the GAS for the registerAccount write. Custody/risk: registration is a real on-chain write whose accountId is a deterministic hash of (verifier, params, hook, backupOwner, timelock); the connected wallet MUST be the backup owner (it witnesses the tx). Default network is mainnet, so a careless write spends real GAS.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet. 2) Inspect: paste an accountId hash -> reads getVerifier/getHook/getBackupOwner/getEscapeTimelock/isEscapeActive from AA core and renders the detail grid (or 'no verifier registered'). 3) Register: choose verifier (defaults to shared Web3Auth verifier), optional verifier params + hook, backup owner (prefilled to connected wallet), and escape timelock in seconds; the UI live-derives the deterministic AccountId the contract will accept and shows it read-only; it blocks register when the backup owner != connected wallet, when the account already has a verifier (re-register reverts), and warns when on mainnet. 4) After registerAccount broadcasts, it polls getVerifier and re-inspects so the inspector flips to the fresh registered state. Exit/recovery: the escape timelock + backup owner is the social-recovery path the account carries forever; this app only sets/reads it, it does not execute recovery.

gaps.title: Escape timelock is the core value but its meaning (social recovery window) is never explained before the user commits it forever
gaps.evidence: The hero copy (locale accountHeroCopy) calls it 'an explicit escape window' and the field hint (timelockHint) only says 'Required timelock in seconds before backup recovery can execute.' Nowhere does the UI explain WHAT escape/backup recovery does — i.e. that after this many seconds the backup owner can seize control of the account if the primary verifier is lost. A first-time user picks the default 2592000 (30 days) with no idea this is a permanent recovery-delay tradeoff (shorter = faster recovery but a thief who compromises the backup owner waits less; longer = safer but slow lockout recovery). The escape-status read (currentEscapeActive -> 'Escape active'/'Inactive') is shown with zero explanation of what an active escape means (a recovery is in progress = the account is being seized).
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add one or two locale sentences under the Escape Timelock input and the Escape Status detail row explaining the recovery model in product terms (e.g. 'If you lose the primary key, the backup owner can take over the account after this delay. Shorter = faster recovery; longer = more protection against a compromised backup owner.' and for status: 'Escape active = a backup recovery is currently in progress for this account.'). No ABI change.

gaps.title: Verifier defaults to the shared Web3Auth verifier but the UI never says what choosing a verifier means for who can sign for the account
gaps.evidence: registerForm.verifierHash defaults to integration.contracts.aaWeb3AuthVerifier and verifierHint says only 'Required. Defaults to the shared Web3Auth verifier.' The verifier IS the authentication authority of the account — it determines what signatures/proofs the account accepts. A user registering an account with this default is delegating auth to a shared Web3Auth contract without the UI ever framing 'this contract decides who can move funds from your account.' verifierParams (the constructor payload that, for Web3Auth, typically binds the account to a specific identity/pubkey) is labeled merely 'Optional constructor payload, encoded as hex' — so the most security-critical binding looks optional/cosmetic.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: relabel/expand the verifier and verifier-params hints to state that the verifier contract controls who can authorize transactions for this account, and that verifier params usually bind the account to your specific identity/key (leaving them empty may produce an account nobody can use or anyone can use, depending on the verifier). Optionally add a one-line 'What is a verifier?' note in the Register card.

gaps.title: 'Lab' framing under-signals that this provisions a real, permanent mainnet account
gaps.evidence: App name 'AA Account Lab' + category 'tools' + feature copy ('This lab keeps optional hook and verifier params flexible...') frames the experience as a sandbox. The only counter-signal is the mainnetCaution alert ('Register Account is a real write against mainnet AA Core and spends GAS'), which appears only when networkDisplay === 'mainnet'. There is no persistent statement that a registered account is a permanent, addressable shell that will hold value.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: keep the mainnet alert but also add a neutral, always-visible one-liner in the Register card hero/subtitle clarifying that registering creates a real, permanent AA account at the derived id (not a throwaway sandbox object).

apps.business_model: A peer-to-peer trustless escrow MARKETPLACE for trading deterministic Neo Abstract Account addresses (the AAAddressMarket contract, mainnet 0xae7afe3a..., domain market.smartwallet.neo). Two user roles: (1) SELLER — owns an AA account (must be its backup owner) and lists the address shell for a price in GAS; (2) BUYER — pays that GAS to acquire control of the AA address. Economic model: the buyer's GAS payment is escrowed in the market contract and released to the seller atomically with the transfer of the AA shell (GAS.transfer + settleListing batched via invokeMultiple); the contract appears to take NO platform fee (price goes seller-ward; no fee arg in createListing). Critically the product is SHELL-ONLY: on sale the verifier/hook/backup-owner config is cleared, so the buyer receives a blank shell at that deterministic address and must reconfigure it. Risk/custody: a buyer whose payment lands but whose settlement does not complete has a refundable pending payment (getPendingPaymentOf -> refundPendingPayment); sellers can reprice or cancel active listings.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet; market hash is prefilled to the canonical AAAddressMarket so the board auto-loads (getListingCount + getListing fan-out). 2) SELL: enter AA contract hash (defaulted), the 20-byte accountId hash you own, a price in GAS (0.01-1000), optional title/metadata; UI pre-checks you are the account's backup owner (getBackupOwner) before createListing. 3) Listing lifecycle: active -> seller may updateListingPrice or cancelListing; -> on buyer settle becomes sold. 4) BUY: select an active listing not your own, set the new backup owner (default = your wallet), Buy -> invokeMultiple{GAS.transfer(price -> market), settleListing(id, buyer, newBackupOwner)}; the AA shell transfers and the seller is paid in one tx. 5) Recovery exit: if you paid but settlement is incomplete, a 'pending refund' chip appears and Refund Pending Payment returns your GAS.

gaps.title: The decisive 'what you actually buy' fact (shell-only; verifier/hook/backup-owner are wiped) is buried in a collapsed details element and absent from the Buy action
gaps.evidence: The README/feature copy is explicit ('the market transfers only the AA shell; verifier, hook, and backup-owner configuration are intentionally cleared on sale; the buyer must reconfigure fresh permissions') — but in the UI this is hidden behind a collapsed <details><summary>{t('feature2Name')}='Shell-Only Transfer'</summary> in PlayArea.tsx (lines 179-182), and the ManageListingCard Buy flow (CardComponent, canBuy branch) shows only a 'New Backup Owner' input + 'Buy Listing' button with NO statement that the buyer is paying GAS for an address whose existing verifier/hook/plugins will be reset to nothing. A buyer scanning a listing (which displays seller, accountId, price, title) reasonably assumes they get a configured/usable account.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: surface the shell-only caveat inline in the Buy panel (ManageListingCard, canBuy branch) as an always-visible note above the Buy button — e.g. 'You are buying only the address shell. Its current verifier, hook, and backup-owner settings are cleared on sale; you must reconfigure control after purchase.' Reuse the existing hubSummary/feature2 locale strings; do not rely on the collapsed details.

gaps.title: Buyer is never shown that their GAS payment escrows in the market and is released to the seller — escrow model invisible at the moment of payment
gaps.evidence: buyAddressListing (utils/aa-market.ts:522-562) batches GAS.transfer(buyer -> market) then settleListing, i.e. funds flow buyer -> market escrow -> seller atomically; the refund path exists because a payment can strand in the market. The hero feature1 'Trustless Escrow' ('Buyers pay GAS into the market and settle only if the AA shell transfer succeeds') states this, but it lives only in the hero/feature list, not at the Buy CTA. The Buy button just says 'Buy Listing' and the price is shown, but nothing at the point of action tells the buyer their GAS goes into market escrow and is released on successful transfer (and is refundable otherwise).
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add a one-line escrow explainer in the Buy panel next to the price (e.g. 'Pays {price} GAS into the market escrow; released to the seller only when the address transfers to you. If settlement fails, use Refund Pending Payment to recover it.'). Pull price from selectedListing.priceGas; reuse marketStepSettlement / feature1 copy.

gaps.title: No-platform-fee economics are implied but never stated; seller cannot see net proceeds vs. price
gaps.evidence: createListing (utils/aa-market.ts:452-482) sends only (aaContractHash, accountIdHash, price, title, metadata) with no fee parameter, and the buy path transfers exactly listing.priceRaw to the market — so the seller receives the full price minus only network GAS, and the platform takes no cut. The Create Listing card collects a price but never tells the seller what they net, and the marketplace never states whether it charges a fee. For a money-handling marketplace, 'does the platform take a cut?' is a basic trust question left unanswered.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy in CreateListingCard: state that the buyer pays the full listed price to the seller and the market charges no platform fee (only network GAS applies). One sentence under the Price input.

gaps.title: Seller-side lifecycle does not surface the buyer's pending-payment / refund state, so a seller cannot reason about a stuck sale
gaps.evidence: getPendingPaymentOf is read per-listing only for the CURRENT wallet (listAddressListings, aa-market.ts:404-422; selectedListingHasPendingRefund in useAAMarketHub.ts:88-96), and the pending/refund chip + Refund button only appear for the payer. A seller viewing their own active listing has no indication that a buyer has a stranded pending payment or that settlement is mid-flight; the only states a seller sees are active/sold/cancelled.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: this is read-only over existing ABI but the contract only exposes getPendingPaymentOf(id, payer) keyed by payer, so a seller can't enumerate buyers — acknowledge that limit and instead add seller-facing copy clarifying that a sale only completes when a buyer settles, and that until then the listing stays 'active'. Avoid implying the seller can see/refund buyer payments.

apps.business_model: A security/admin control room for the OWNER of a Neo Abstract Account (UnifiedSmartWalletV3, core.smartwallet.neo). The user is the account's backup owner who needs to rotate the account's authentication (verifier) or policy (hook) bindings — e.g. migrate to a new auth scheme or change a guard policy. Value: safely inspect the live verifier/hook/backup-owner and perform a TIMELOCKED two-phase rotation (propose -> wait out timelock -> confirm, or cancel) so a single compromised key can't instantly hijack the account's auth. Economic model: no fee/reward; cost is GAS per write. Custody/risk: only the backup owner may rotate bindings (contract-enforced; UI blocks non-owner). The timelock is the safety primitive — it gives the real owner a window to cancel a malicious pending rotation.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet + paste accountId hash -> Refresh State reads getVerifier/getHook/getBackupOwner + hasPendingVerifierUpdate/hasPendingHookUpdate + their unlock times. 2) The UI shows current bindings and a 'configured' chip once read. 3) Rotate verifier: enter new verifier hash + optional params -> updateVerifier PROPOSES the change (enters timelock). 4) A pending banner shows the unlock time; when the timelock elapses the owner clicks Confirm (confirmVerifierUpdate) to finalize, or Cancel (cancelVerifierUpdate) to abort. Same propose/confirm/cancel cycle for hook. 5) Non-backup-owner wallets are blocked from all writes with guidance. No fund custody — this only governs the account's permission boundary.

gaps.title: The button says 'Update Verifier'/'Update Hook' but the action only PROPOSES a timelocked change — the two-phase model is not signalled until after the user pays for the propose tx
gaps.evidence: submitVerifier/submitHook call updateVerifier/updateHook which (per the pending-update state machine: hasPendingVerifierUpdate, getPendingVerifierUpdateTime, confirmVerifierUpdate/cancelVerifierUpdate) START a timelocked proposal — the success message even says 'Verifier update proposed — confirm after the timelock' (locale successVerifier). But the CTA is labeled simply 'Update Verifier' (locale updateVerifier) with no pre-action hint that this is step 1 of 2 and that the change won't take effect until a later Confirm after a delay. A user expects 'Update' to be immediate.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: relabel or annotate the propose CTA (e.g. 'Propose Verifier Update' or keep label + add a hint under the button: 'This proposes a change; it takes effect only after the timelock elapses and you Confirm.'). Add a short two-phase explainer above the Update Verifier/Update Hook cards. Locale-only.

gaps.title: Pending banner shows an unlock time but never explains WHY the timelock exists (the security value prop is invisible)
gaps.evidence: The pending block renders pendingVerifierTitle + pendingUnlockText ('Timelock elapsed — confirm to finalize.' / 'Unlocks at {time}.') with Confirm/Cancel, but no copy explains that the delay is the protection: it gives the owner time to Cancel a malicious rotation. feature3 even mislabels the model as 'Direct Wallet — Writes go straight to the shared AA core', contradicting the actual delayed two-phase flow.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add one sentence to the pending banner or risk-copy explaining the timelock is a safety window during which a malicious or mistaken rotation can be cancelled before it takes effect; fix the misleading feature3 'Direct Wallet/Writes go straight' copy to describe the propose->timelock->confirm model. Locale-only.

apps.business_model: An operator/developer console for the GASLESS-transaction side of Neo Account Abstraction: a paymaster-sponsored relay. The user is someone who wants an AA account's transactions to be paid for by a paymaster (sponsor) rather than the account itself, and submitted via a shared relay endpoint (/api/aa/relay) instead of a direct on-chain send. Value: (1) Check Sponsorship — is this AA address eligible for paymaster GAS coverage under a given dApp scope, and how much daily budget remains; (2) Request Sponsorship — ask the paymaster to cover a GAS amount for this scope; (3) Submit Relay Payload — push a relay-ready AA meta-transaction through the relay so the paymaster fronts the fee. Economic model: a third-party paymaster pays the network GAS on the user's behalf, subject to per-dApp eligibility and a daily GAS limit (the result surfaces remaining/dailyLimit). Off-chain relay/paymaster infra is the backend; the contract anchor is core.smartwallet.neo.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Enter the AA address. 2) Check Sponsorship (optional dApp id scope) -> shows Eligible/Not eligible + remaining-of-daily-limit, or a service-unavailable line. 3) Request Sponsorship for a GAS amount (default 0.1) -> approved/denied. 4) Edit the relay payload JSON (defaults to a metaInvocation skeleton), set dApp id, Submit Relay Payload -> the relay forwards it and returns a relay response. The result line promotes the human answer (eligible / remaining budget / submitted) and collapses the raw JSON. Honest degradation: when the relay/paymaster edge is not configured, known failure markers map to 'Sponsorship service is currently unavailable.'

gaps.title: The core value prop — 'someone else pays your GAS' — is never stated; the UI reads as opaque payload plumbing, not gasless sponsorship
gaps.evidence: Hero copy (relayHeroCopy) is 'Check sponsorship, request paymaster support, and submit relay-ready payloads from one guarded operator surface' and the card is titled 'Sponsor Preflight'. Nowhere does it explain in user terms that a paymaster pays the network GAS so the AA account can transact without holding GAS, nor what 'Sponsor Amount' actually buys. A first-time, non-expert user cannot tell why they'd use this app vs. a normal send. The 'Sponsor Amount' field hint ('GAS amount requested from the paymaster for this AA scope') presumes the reader already understands paymaster sponsorship.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: add a plain-language line to the hero/'Sponsor Preflight' card stating the benefit — e.g. 'A paymaster can pay the network GAS for this account so it can transact without holding GAS. Check whether this address is covered, request coverage, then submit the relayed transaction.' Locale-only.

gaps.title: 'Request Sponsorship' commits a sponsor amount with no statement of who pays it, whether the user owes anything, or what the daily limit means before acting
gaps.evidence: requestSponsor sends sponsorAmount (default 0.1 GAS) to aa.requestSponsorship. The only budget context (remaining/dailyLimit) is surfaced AFTER a check, via sponsorEligibleSummary ('Eligible — {remaining} GAS of {dailyLimit} remaining today.'). Before requesting, the user has no framing of whether 'Sponsor Amount' is something they pay, something the paymaster grants, or how it relates to the daily limit. For a money/credit flow, the direction of value should be explicit pre-commit.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add a hint near the Sponsor Amount / Request button clarifying the direction of value (the paymaster grants this GAS to cover the account's fees; it draws against a shared daily limit; the user is not charged for requesting). Encourage Check Sponsorship first to see remaining budget. Locale-only.

gaps.title: Relay vs. direct on-chain mental model is unclear — the user can't tell what actually happens on-chain when they Submit Relay Payload
gaps.evidence: submitRelay POSTs the payload JSON to an off-chain relay (relayUrlDisplay = '/api/aa/relay') which then submits the AA meta-transaction; this is fundamentally different from the wallet-signed direct invokes in the other AA apps. The UI shows the endpoint as a hero fact and returns a relay response, but never frames that the actual on-chain transaction is broadcast by the relayer/paymaster (not the user's wallet) — leaving trust-transparency thin: the user can't easily tie the relay response to a verifiable on-chain txid/outcome.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add copy explaining that Submit sends the payload to a relayer that broadcasts it on-chain on the account's behalf (paid by the paymaster), and, if the relay response carries a txid/hash, render it as the verifiable on-chain reference in the result line rather than only raw JSON.

apps.business_model: A delegation/security tool for the owner of a Neo Abstract Account who wants to grant a SCOPED session key — a temporary, limited credential that lets an automation/bot/dApp act for the account WITHOUT the master key. Backed by SessionKeyVerifier (mainnet 0x3ba83334..., sessionkey.smartwallet.neo) configured via aaCore.callVerifier('setSessionKey'). Value: generate a fresh P-256 keypair locally in the browser, then bind its PUBLIC key to exactly one target contract + one allowed method, with an expiry and (mainnet) a GAS spending cap and human label — then hand the PRIVATE key to the automation. Economic model: no fee; cost is GAS per setSessionKey/clearSessionKey write. The optional paymaster sponsorship lane (check/request) can cover that GAS. Risk/custody: the private key is generated client-side and shown once for the user to copy (the app never stores it); the security guarantees are the method scope, expiry, and spending limit; the owner can revoke (clearSessionKey) and inspect the live key (getSessionKey) and accrued spend (getSpentAmount).
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet, enter account seed/hash (live-derives accountId). 2) Generate Key -> creates a browser-local keypair; the public key fills the form and the private key is shown once with show/hide + copy. 3) (Optional) Check/Request paymaster sponsorship to cover the config GAS. 4) Configure scope: bind session public key -> target contract + allowed method (blank = any) + expiry (quick-picks +1h/+24h/+7d) + (mainnet) spending limit in GAS + description -> Configure Session Key calls callVerifier(setSessionKey); the app polls getSessionKey and only flips to 'configured' once the verifier confirms the stored key. 5) Lifecycle out: Inspect Session Key reads the live key from the verifier; Revoke Session Key calls clearSessionKey. The user then deploys the private key into their automation, which can transact within the scope until expiry/limit/revoke.

gaps.title: The one-time private key is the most sensitive object in the app but is presented with no warning about its blast radius (it can spend within the granted scope until expiry/limit/revoke)
gaps.evidence: Generate Key reveals the private key once (privateKeyReady = 'Ready for one-time copy', show/copy controls). The accompanying copy never warns that (a) this private key grants real signing power over the account within the configured scope, (b) it is shown only once and the app does not store it, and (c) anyone who obtains it can act as the session key until expiry/spending-limit/revoke. For a credential that authorizes spending, this absence of a security warning is a trust gap.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add a security caution next to the private-key export (e.g. 'This private key can authorize transactions for the account within the scope you set below, until it expires or you revoke it. It is shown once and never stored — copy it somewhere safe and share it only with the automation you trust.'). Locale-only.

gaps.title: Spending limit is set but the accrued spend against it (getSpentAmount) is never read or shown — the budget half of the safety model is invisible
gaps.evidence: The mainnet config sets a GAS spending limit (normalizeSpendingLimit, buildSessionKeyArgs), and SessionKeyVerifier exposes getSpentAmount/1 (confirmed in the contract method report) — but neither inspectSessionKey nor the detail/onchain views read or display spent-vs-limit. inspectSessionKey only dumps raw getSessionKey JSON into onChainSession. So an owner who imposed a cap cannot see how much of it has been consumed, which is the entire point of a spending limit.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only over existing ABI: in inspectSessionKey, also chain.read('getSpentAmount', [accountId], {scriptHash: sessionVerifier}) and render 'Spent X / Limit Y GAS' in the session detail / on-chain panel. Pure added read; no contract change.

gaps.title: Inspect shows raw JSON of the on-chain session key instead of decoding the scope (target/method/expiry/spent) the user can verify
gaps.evidence: inspectSessionKey sets onChainSession to JSON.stringify(getSessionKey result) and PlayArea renders it as a <code> blob (session-onchain__value). The user cannot easily verify the on-chain truth that the product promises (which contract/method the key is bound to, when it expires, how much it has spent) — exactly the 'what did I delegate?' question the code comment claims this view answers.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: decode the getSessionKey array (and getSessionKeyMetadata/getSpentAmount) into labeled fields (target contract, allowed method, expiry as a date, spending limit, spent) and render them in the existing detail-row layout instead of raw JSON. Read-only decode.

gaps.title: 'Allowed Method' blank = ANY method is a major scope-widening default that is signalled only as a faint 'Any method' label
gaps.evidence: normalizedAllowedMethod returns t('anyMethod') when allowedMethod is blank, and configureSessionKey forwards that. Leaving the field empty therefore grants the session key permission to call ANY method on the target contract — a much broader delegation — but the only signal is the placeholder/'Any method' scope metric, with no caution that an empty method removes the per-method restriction.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: when allowedMethod is empty, show an inline note that the session key will be allowed to call any method on the target contract, and recommend specifying a single method to narrow the scope. Locale-only.

apps.business_model: A developer/issuer tool: a OneGate-loadable, walletless-until-execute console that lets a Neo builder mint a NEP-17 fungible token from a single audited, on-chain template (tpl.nep17.asset.v1) governed by the shared MiniAppFactory registry. The user supplies only init parameters (name, symbol, decimals 0-8, initial supply, owner, treasury, mintable). Economic model: the user pays only the Neo network/system GAS fee for the deployFromTemplate transaction (estimated live via estimateFactoryFeeGas in factoryChain.ts); there is no app-level fee or revenue capture, and no NEF/manifest upload (the factory deploys a preloaded, governed artifact). The deterministic SHA-256 plan digest is wallet-signable as an issuer attestation. Custody: the deployed token's owner/treasury are whatever addresses the issuer typed; the factory itself takes no custody.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Open the console (testnet by default per neo-manifest.default_network). 2) Fill the NEP-17 form; the connected wallet auto-seeds owner+treasury. 3) Generate template plan -> validates inputs, live-reads getTemplate() to verify the artifact is preloaded on-chain, computes a deterministic digest+packageId. 4) (optional) Sign the plan digest with the wallet as an issuer commitment. 5) Deploy via factory -> ctx.services.chain.invoke('deployFromTemplate', ...) waiting on the TokenDeployed event; the factory deploys the preloaded artifact and records a DeploymentRecord; the deployed contract hash is read back authoritatively. 6) The token now exists on-chain; the issuer binds domain/catalog metadata (manual step) and shares the OneGate launch URL. 'On-chain creations' lists prior deployments with their contract hash. Exit/recovery: the artifact is deployed once and is non-refundable; there is no in-app teardown (a token is permanent).

gaps.title: Headline promise 'Create NEP-17 assets' is unachievable on the default network — deploy is permanently blocked because no artifact is preloaded
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description='Create NEP-17 assets from audited on-chain templates' and the hero subtitle (asset-factory/src/locale/messages.ts:7) promise asset creation, with default_network=neo-n3-testnet. But a live read of the configured testnet factory (0x03a7c8fc724a575ee739c919ed52cb5e2a2bdc49) getTemplate('tpl.nep17.asset.v1') returns HasArtifact=false, so factoryPlan.ts makeExecution() sets execution.available=false with blockedReasonKey='artifactNotRegistered'. A newcomer following the headline can fill the form and Generate, but the Deploy button is always disabled with 'the template artifact is not registered on-chain yet'. The product reads as 'create a token' while the default-network deliverable is only a signed plan + record-only entry.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: when execution.available is false because presence!=='present', reframe the hero/value-prop to set honest expectations before the user invests effort — e.g. a one-line banner in the hero status area ('On {network}, deployable artifacts are preloaded by a factory admin; this template is metadata-only here. Switch to a network where the artifact is registered, or export a signed plan.') keyed off the live artifactPresence already in state. Optionally surface a per-network availability hint next to the network <select> in FactoryPlayArea.tsx so the user picks a network where deploy actually works.

gaps.title: Network fee (the only cost) is hidden until deploy is unblocked, so it is never shown on the path the user actually hits
gaps.evidence: runtime.tsx refreshFeeEstimate() returns early unless plan.publishable && plan.execution.available, and FactoryPlayArea.tsx:417 only renders the 'Estimated network fee' row when feeEstimate is non-empty. Because deploy is blocked on the default network (artifact metadata-only), feeEstimate stays empty and the user never sees what the deployment would cost. The factory's entire economic model for the user is 'you pay GAS for one deployment' — and that single fact is invisible.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: show the cost model explicitly even when blocked — either a static doc line ('Deploying from a template costs only the Neo network fee; no app fee is charged') in the deployHonesty note (already at FactoryPlayArea.tsx:613), or attempt the fee estimate whenever the plan is publishable (drop the execution.available precondition for the read-only estimate, since estimateFactoryFeeGas is a harmless test-invoke).

gaps.title: Sign step's purpose in the lifecycle is unclear — a newcomer cannot tell why to sign a plan that cannot be deployed
gaps.evidence: The actions row offers Copy plan / Sign template plan / Deploy (FactoryPlayArea.tsx:457-477). signPlanDescription (shared messages.ts:48) explains signing mechanically ('Signs the deterministic template-plan digest') but not its product role — as an off-chain issuer attestation that can travel with an exported plan for later/governed deployment. With deploy blocked, the user is left with a signed digest and no obvious next move.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: clarify in signPlanDescription / a hint under the Sign button that the signature is a portable issuer commitment to these exact parameters, useful for handing the plan to a factory admin or for an off-chain audit trail when in-app deploy is not yet available.

apps.business_model: Same factory engine as asset-factory, specialized to kind='nep11': a creator/issuer tool to launch a NEP-11 collection (collections, tickets, badges, soulbound drops) from one audited on-chain template (tpl.nep11.collection.v1). User supplies init params: collection name, symbol, max supply (1-1,000,000), royalty in bps (0-1000, surfaced as a % helper), HTTPS metadata base URI, owner, and a transferable/soulbound toggle (transferPolicy). Economic model: user pays only the network GAS for deployFromTemplate; the royaltyBps is a creator-economics parameter baked into the collection (a % of each sale routed to the creator), not an app fee. No artifact upload; factory deploys a governed preloaded artifact. Custody: collection owner is the issuer's address; factory takes no custody.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Open console (testnet default). 2) Fill collection form; wallet auto-seeds owner. 3) Generate plan -> validate + live HasArtifact check + deterministic digest. 4) (optional) Sign digest. 5) Deploy via factory ('deployFromTemplate', wait TokenDeployed) -> collection contract deployed, DeploymentRecord stored, deployed hash read back. 6) Bind domain/catalog metadata, share OneGate URL; 'On-chain creations' lists prior collections. Exit: collection is permanent; royalty/transfer policy are fixed at deploy from the chosen params.

gaps.title: 'Create NEP-11 collections' headline is unfulfillable on the default network — artifact is metadata-only so deploy is permanently blocked
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description='Create NEP-11 collections from audited on-chain templates' and hero subtitle (nft-factory/src/locale/messages.ts:7) promise collection creation; default_network=testnet. Live read of getTemplate('tpl.nep11.collection.v1') on the configured testnet factory returns HasArtifact=false -> factoryPlan.ts blocks execution with artifactNotRegistered. The Deploy button is always disabled; the app delivers only a signed plan / record-only entry, not the advertised collection.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: same remedy as asset-factory — an honest hero-level network-availability banner driven by the live artifactPresence already in state, and/or a network-availability hint by the network selector, so the user understands the deployable artifact is admin-preloaded per network and can choose a network where it exists or knowingly export a plan.

gaps.title: Royalty parameter is shown as a creator setting but the business consequence (who gets paid, on what, by whom) is not framed
gaps.evidence: FactoryPlayArea.tsx:354 renders the Royalty bps input with royaltyHelper ('{bps} bps = {percent}% of each sale', shared messages.ts:257), which states the math but not the economic model — that this is an on-sale fee paid to the collection owner enforced at the marketplace/transfer layer, and that it is fixed at deploy. A first-time creator cannot tell whether royalty is collected automatically, by whom, or that it is immutable after launch.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: extend royaltyHelper or add a one-line hint under the field clarifying that royalty is a marketplace-honored cut routed to the collection owner on secondary sales and is fixed at deployment. Likewise label the transferable/soulbound toggle's consequence (soulbound = non-transferable forever) at the control.

apps.business_model: Same factory engine, kind='miniapp': a developer tool to register a new platform miniapp instance on-chain from one of four governed templates (reward-vault, ticket-pass, certificate, oracle-console). Unlike the asset/NFT factories, the designed on-chain outcome is a REGISTRY RECORD (createMiniAppFromTemplate), not a contract artifact deployment — so it does not require a preloaded NEF/manifest artifact, only that the template id is registered on the factory. User supplies appId (miniapp-<slug>), app name, template kind, admin address, and oracle/OneGate capability toggles; the plan also emits a catalog patch the operator syncs to the platform registry. Economic model: user pays only the network GAS for the register call; no app fee.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Open console (testnet default). 2) Fill miniapp form; wallet auto-seeds admin. 3) Generate plan -> validate + live template-registration check + deterministic digest + a catalog patch. 4) (optional) Sign digest. 5) Register on-chain ('createMiniAppFromTemplate', wait MiniAppCreated) -> factory stores a MiniAppRecord (verified live: miniAppCount=1 on testnet). 6) Sync the generated catalog patch to Notion/platform registry (warned via catalog_registration_required) and share the OneGate URL. 'On-chain creations' lists registered instances. Exit: the record is an append-only registry entry; the underlying app is then wired by the operator.

gaps.title: The two on-chain outcomes (record vs contract) are conflated by shared action copy, blurring what the user is actually getting
gaps.evidence: The miniapp factory's execute correctly produces a registry record (factoryPlan.ts makeExecution outcome='registry-record', confirmingEvent='MiniAppCreated') and the button uses executeRecordAction='Register on-chain' (FactoryPlayArea.tsx:475). However the surrounding shell still calls this 'Template deployment plan' (publishPackage, shared messages.ts:61) and the section heading 'Deploy checklist' / step 'Create platform miniapp from template' sits next to deployHonesty copy written for artifact deployment ('It submits a preloaded template ID...and blocks execution until that contract is configured', shared messages.ts:72). A first-time developer cannot tell that here they are creating an instance RECORD (a catalog/registry entry to be wired later), not deploying a running contract.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: override the miniapp-specific strings in miniapp-factory/src/locale/messages.ts (publishPackage, deployChecklist, deployHonesty) to say 'Register a miniapp instance record' and explain that this creates an on-chain registry entry + catalog patch that the operator then wires — distinct from deploying a token contract. The per-app locale already overrides title/subtitle/doc bodies, so this is consistent with the existing pattern.

gaps.title: Post-register lifecycle (sync catalog patch, then app goes live) is only a buried warning, not a visible next-step
gaps.evidence: buildMiniAppPlan() always pushes warning 'catalog_registration_required' and emits a catalogPatch in the payload (factoryPlan.ts:715,740), but the UI surfaces this only as a generic warning bullet (warnCatalogRegistration, shared messages.ts:137) and the patch is hidden inside the collapsed JSON disclosure. After a successful register the user sees a txid but no guidance that the instance is not usable until the catalog patch is synced — the record-only deliverable feels finished when it is not.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: after lastTxid is set for the miniapp kind, render an explicit 'Next: sync the catalog patch to the platform registry to make this miniapp launchable' step (the patch is already in currentPlan.payload), e.g. a dedicated affordance to copy just the catalogPatch object rather than the whole package JSON.

apps.business_model: A consumer identity/naming utility: register and manage human-readable .neo domain names that map to a Neo wallet address, backed by the live NNS contract (0x50ac1c37690cc2cfc594472833cf57505d5f46de). A domain is an NEP-11 NFT the holder fully owns (transfer/sell/manage). Economic model: the user pays a length-based registration price in GAS per year (getPrice(nameLength)/1e8), shorter names cost more ('premium'); renewal costs the same length-based price for +1 year; the GAS is paid to the NNS contract. Custody: the domain NFT is held by the user's wallet; the app holds nothing. Lifecycle facts: 1-year term, expiry tracked, renew-before-expiry to keep ownership, set an address record (target), or transfer the NFT.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet, search a name -> live isAvailable + getPrice reads; result shows Available (with 'Cost: N GAS / year' and a Register button) or Taken (with the current owner's N-address). 2) Register -> chain.invoke('register', name, owner) waiting on Transfer; optimistic add to 'My Domains'. 3) Manage a domain -> set target address (setRecord type 16) or transfer the NFT to another address (both validate N3 address format first). 4) Renew -> discloses the GAS cost in a confirm prompt ('Renew {name} for {cost} GAS (+1 year)?') before the paid tx. 5) Expiry surfaced per domain and an 'Expiring' counter in the hero (30-day window). Exit/recovery: ownership is the NFT itself — transfer to exit; lapse renewal to release.

gaps.title: Expired domains are listed identically to active ones with no 'expired / re-register' affordance
gaps.evidence: DomainManagement.tsx renders every owned domain with the same Manage/Renew actions and only an 'Expires: <date>' line; useNeoNS.ts expiringSoon counts only future-but-near expiries (remaining>0 && <30d) and explicitly excludes already-expired domains, so a domain whose expiry has passed shows a past date with no visual distinction or guidance. The business model hinges on 'renew before expiry to keep ownership' (step4), but the post-expiry state has no dedicated UI.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: in DomainManagement.tsx flag rows where domain.expiry>0 && domain.expiry<Date.now() with an 'Expired' badge and a hint (renew may no longer guarantee ownership; the name may be re-claimable), reusing the existing expiry data already in state.

apps.business_model: A governance/yield staking surface over the shared PlatformAnchor engine (testnet 0xab079b4f...; mainnet 0x02beeef6...). A team/community first REGISTERS a custom anchor (appId custom-anchor:slug:nonce) for a 1-GAS prepaid fee and becomes its admin, choosing a mode: Trust (mode 1, voting — staked NEO is routed through the anchor's 21 deterministic AA agent accounts to vote for council candidates) or Profit (mode 2, yield). Users then stake whole NEO into an anchor (NEO transfer with memo 'stake:<appId>'), which is held by the contract and routed to agents; the GAS those NEO holdings generate (harvested via harvestRewards / topped up via fundRewards into the per-anchor rewardReserve) is distributed pro-rata (getRewardPerNeo) and claimable as GAS (claimRewards). Users redeem NEO back (withdraw) and reclaim over/failed deposits (withdrawCredit). Custody: the contract custodies staked NEO and the GAS reward reserve, scoped per anchor appId. Who-pays-whom: stakers supply NEO -> anchor agents vote/earn GAS -> stakers claim GAS pro-rata; the anchor admin manages agents and may fund rewards.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Arrive via a OneGate link carrying anchorAppId, OR discover/select a registered anchor, OR register a new one (1 GAS, pick Trust/Profit, become admin). 2) For a registered anchor: read getAppMode + getTotalStaked/getRewardReserve/getAgentCount + your getUserStake/getPendingRewards. 3) Stake whole NEO (transfer memo 'stake:<appId>', wait AnchorStakeChanged). 4) Over time, claim accrued GAS rewards (claimRewards, wait AnchorRewardsClaimed). 5) Redeem NEO anytime (withdraw, wait AnchorStakeChanged). 6) Recover any stranded contract credit (NEO/GAS) via withdrawCredit. Admin-only (explicitly out of this user dApp): registerAgents, setAgentCandidate, transferAgentNeo, voteAgent. Exit/recovery: redeem returns staked NEO; contract-credit recovery card returns over/failed deposits.

gaps.title: Manifest promises 'create 21 AA agent accounts' but the app never provisions agents — a self-registered anchor is born with 0 agents and cannot vote/earn
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description: 'Register one anchor, create 21 AA agent accounts, then let users stake NEO...'. The register action (main.tsx:324) calls only registerCustomAnchorApp; it never calls registerAgents (which exists in PlatformAnchor.manifest.json). registerAgentsNote (locale messages.ts:113) admits 'a new anchor starts with 0 of its 21 AA agents... provisioned by the anchor operator (admin console)'. So the headline workflow step ('create 21 AA agent accounts') has no UI here, and a freshly registered Trust anchor with 0 agents routes no votes and generates no GAS — the staking/reward business model is inert until an off-app admin step happens.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: align the value-prop with what the app actually does — reframe the manifest/hero copy to 'Register an anchor and let users stake; agent provisioning is handled in the admin console' (do NOT claim agent creation here), and after a successful register surface a prominent 'This anchor has 0/21 agents — staking earns nothing until the operator provisions agents' callout (the agentCount is already read into state) instead of leaving it as a buried note.

gaps.title: Stake is not gated on agentCount>0 and the 'no agents = no rewards' warning is hidden in a collapsed panel — users can stake NEO into an anchor that earns nothing
gaps.evidence: PlayArea.tsx stakeDisabled = busy || !anchorInputValid || !amountValid — there is NO check on agentCount. agentCount is shown in the hero facts (PlayArea.tsx:198) but the only explanation that 0 agents means staking earns nothing (registerAgentsNote) lives inside the collapsed <details> Register panel (PlayArea.tsx:469), which a user who arrives via a OneGate link or 'Use' from discovery never opens. A user can therefore stake real NEO into a 0-agent anchor (verified: live testnet anchor getTotalRewardReserve=0) and see Claimable GAS stay 0 with no warning.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: when anchorLinked && !anchorNotRegistered && agentCount===0, show an inline warning above the Stake button ('This anchor has no AA agents yet — staked NEO will not vote or earn GAS until the operator provisions agents') and/or require an explicit confirm before staking. The agentCount needed for this is already in PlayArea state.

gaps.title: Where claimable GAS comes from is never explained, so the reward side of the model is illegible before users commit NEO
gaps.evidence: The UI shows 'Claimable GAS', 'Reward reserve', and a Claim GAS button (PlayArea.tsx:329-333, locale claimDescription:62 'Claim accumulated GAS rewards') but no copy anywhere explains the source: staked NEO routed through agents generates/earns GAS that is harvested (harvestRewards) or funded (fundRewards) into the per-anchor reserve and distributed pro-rata by getRewardPerNeo. A first-time staker cannot tell whether rewards are guaranteed, market-driven, admin-funded, or proportional to their stake.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: add a short reward-model explainer near the metrics card or in the routing-details panel ('Staked NEO votes via the anchor's agents; the GAS those holdings generate is pooled in the reward reserve and shared pro-rata by stake. Rewards depend on the anchor being funded/harvested by its operator.'). Read getRewardPerNeo (already in ABI) to show the current per-NEO reward rate so the yield is concrete.

gaps.title: Trust vs Profit mode is a one-word toggle with no explanation of the economic difference at registration
gaps.evidence: The register panel offers two toggle buttons labeled 'Trust (voting)' and 'Profit (yield)' (PlayArea.tsx:441-460, locale registerModeTrust/registerModeProfit). The ABI distinguishes mode 1 vs 2 (getAppMode), and the discovery list renders modeTrust/modeProfit one-word tags, but nothing explains what choosing each mode means for the anchor's stakers (how NEO is routed, how/whether GAS accrues, voting vs pure yield). An admin registering an anchor — a permanent, fee-bearing choice — cannot make an informed decision.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: add a one-line description under each mode toggle (Trust = staked NEO is routed to vote for council candidates via the 21 agents; Profit = NEO is staked for GAS yield without governance voting) and mirror it in the discovery list tags so users browsing anchors understand what they are joining.

apps.business_model: TrustAnchor is a user-facing NEO staking product on the shared PlatformAnchor contract (mode 1, category=governance). The user is a NEO holder who wants GAS yield without running their own voting setup. Value: deposit whole NEO (stake() via NEO transfer with memo `stake:miniapp-trustanchor`), the protocol's 21 AA 'anchor agents' hold and vote that NEO for Neo council candidates, the GAS those votes generate is funded into a reward reserve (fundRewards/harvestRewards) and distributed pro-rata to stakers via a getRewardPerNeo accumulator; the user claims accrued GAS (claimRewards) and can redeem principal at any time (withdraw). Custody: NEO sits in PlatformAnchor; no app fee is taken in the UI (tag 'zero-fee'). Economic model = pass-through Neo voting rewards (GAS) earned on staked NEO, distributed when the operator funds the reserve — NOT a fixed/guaranteed rate. withdrawCredit recovers a bare NEO deposit (no stake memo). Routing of the 21 agents is operator-only and lives in TrustAnchor Admin.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet. 2) See my stake, claimable GAS, total NEO tracked, reward reserve, and the lifetime GAS/NEO rate. 3) Enter a whole-NEO amount and Stake (NEO transfer with `stake:` memo into PlatformAnchor). 4) Over time GAS accrues as the agents' votes generate rewards and the reserve is funded; the user periodically Claims GAS (claimRewards). 5) Redeem principal whenever desired (withdraw returns whole NEO). 6) Exit/recovery: full redeem returns staked NEO; a bare NEO transfer that missed the stake memo shows as 'Claimable NEO' and is recovered via Recover NEO (withdrawCredit). The agent-routing lifecycle (move NEO between agents, set candidate, sync vote) is intentionally out of this app — operator-only in TrustAnchor Admin.

gaps.title: Yield source and no-guarantee nature are never explained — newcomer can't tell why staking earns GAS or whether it's fixed
gaps.evidence: The only yield copy is stakeNeoDesc 'start earning distributed GAS rewards' (locale/messages.ts:122) and a raw 'GAS / NEO (lifetime)' accumulator shown in the route aside (PlayArea.tsx:306, rewardPerNeoDisplay). Nothing tells the user that GAS comes from the 21 anchor agents voting the staked NEO for Neo council candidates, that rewards are only distributed when the reward reserve is funded (fundRewards/harvestRewards in the ABI), and that there is no fixed APR. A first-time staker sees 'Reward Reserve' and 'GAS/NEO lifetime' but no causal story, so the value prop reads as an unexplained black box.
gaps.fix: Add a short 'How you earn' explainer block (1-2 lines + the existing details/routing-model section) stating: your staked NEO is voted by the 21 anchor agents; the GAS those votes generate is funded into the reward reserve and split across stakers by share of total NEO; rewards are variable and only accrue when the reserve is funded. Frontend-only copy + reuse existing rewardReserveDisplay/rewardPerNeoDisplay reads.

gaps.title: No effective-rate context — lifetime 'GAS/NEO' figure is not actionable and reserve is buried in the collapsed aside
gaps.evidence: rewardPerNeoDisplay is a lifetime cumulative GAS-per-NEO number (main.tsx:86-93) shown only inside the route-state aside under label 'GAS / NEO (lifetime)' (PlayArea.tsx:305-308). A user evaluating whether to stake cannot derive any forward-looking expectation from a lifetime accumulator, and the reward reserve (the pool the next claims draw from) is in the same low-prominence aside rather than near the Stake CTA.
gaps.fix: Surface 'Reward Reserve' (claimable GAS pool size) as a top-line hero/stat chip near the Stake action and label the GAS/NEO figure clearly as 'cumulative GAS distributed per NEO since launch' so it is not mistaken for a current rate. Optionally show pendingRewards growth on refresh. Reads already exist (rewardReserveDisplay).

gaps.title: TrustAnchor vs ProfitAnchor are indistinguishable to a user — no surfaced reason to pick the governance app over the DeFi app
gaps.evidence: TrustAnchor (mode 1, category governance) and ProfitAnchor (mode 2, category defi) share the same PlatformAnchor contract, the same operations (stake/withdraw/claimRewards), an identical user hook (useTrustAnchor vs useProfitAnchor differ only in APP_ID/comments per diff), and the same hero line 'Stake. Redeem. Claim.' / 'Stake NEO, redeem NEO, and claim GAS rewards.' (both messages.ts heroTitle/heroDescription). A user browsing both apps cannot tell what is different or which to use; the governance vs profit-policy distinction lives only in the architecture/docs copy of the admin tooling.
gaps.fix: Differentiate the hero/kicker copy: position TrustAnchor explicitly as the governance-aligned anchor (votes follow a council-stability/trust policy) vs ProfitAnchor as the yield-maximizing anchor, and state they are separate pools tracking separate routes. Pure locale copy change; no logic.

gaps.title: Redeem (withdraw) is presented as instant with no timing/availability framing
gaps.evidence: withdrawNeo invokes withdraw() and waits for AnchorStakeChanged (useTrustAnchor.ts:350-369); the UI labels it 'Redeem NEO' with no statement about whether redemption is immediate, whether unclaimed GAS is forfeited or auto-claimed on redeem, or any lock/cooldown. A staker cannot tell the exit terms before committing principal.
gaps.fix: Add one line under the Redeem control: 'Redeem returns your NEO immediately; claim your GAS first or it stays claimable.' (verify auto-claim vs separate-claim against the contract via read-only RPC and word accordingly). Copy-only.

apps.business_model: TrustAnchor Admin is the operator-only console for the 21-agent NEO voting route behind TrustAnchor. The user is the TrustAnchor operator (platform admin() or per-app getAppAdmin). It does exactly three privileged things over the shared PlatformAnchor contract: move whole NEO between two of the app's 21 AA agent accounts (transferAgentNeo), set an agent's council candidate public key (setAgentCandidate), and sync the selected agent's on-chain vote (voteAgent). No user funds are taken or paid here; it changes only governance exposure — which council candidates the staked NEO votes for, which in turn affects the GAS the user pool earns. The deliberate, manual-only design ('no auto rebalance') is the trust promise. Vote sync additionally requires the AA agent witness, not just the admin witness.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Operator connects the TrustAnchor operator wallet; admin()/getAppAdmin gate the console (non-operators get a read-only banner). 2) Review the live route map: selected route, agents N/21, tracked NEO, reserve. 3) Move NEO from one agent to another (transferAgentNeo) to rebalance allocation across candidates. 4) Update an agent's candidate public key when the council set changes (setAgentCandidate). 5) Sync the chosen agent's vote as a separate transaction (voteAgent), which also needs that agent's AA witness. Money lifecycle: no deposit/withdraw of user funds; only intra-protocol agent-to-agent NEO movement and vote pointer changes.

gaps.title: Operator never sees per-agent NEO balances, so 'Move NEO' is a blind transfer
gaps.evidence: The Move-NEO card asks for from-agent, to-agent, and amount (PlayArea.tsx:192-229) but the agent directory only lists agent id + account address (PlayArea.tsx:296-310); no per-agent staked/held NEO is shown. The contract exposes getAgent(appId, id) (returns a Map) and the hook already calls it in loadAgents (useTrustAnchor.ts:251-292) but the admin app uses a static TRUSTANCHOR_AGENT_ACCOUNTS list and discards balances. An operator can submit a move larger than the source agent holds or to the wrong agent with no visibility, which the contract will then revert opaquely.

apps.business_model: A free (gas-only) confidential-messaging app for any Neo X (EVM) wallet holder, backed by MiniAppMessageEVM (0xd1906192…) + the Morpheus confidential oracle. User = sender or recipient with an EVM wallet. Two products in one: (1) recipient-only — sender encrypts to the oracle key, ciphertext is stored on-chain, and ONLY the designated recipient can decrypt off-chain by proving wallet ownership via a personal_sign reveal statement; plaintext never touches the chain (message-logic.ts:1-12,78-92). (2) time-locked — message stays sealed until unlockTime, after which ANYONE may trigger requestReveal and the relayer/oracle decrypts and posts the plaintext PUBLICLY on-chain (message-logic.ts:31-35,131-142). No protocol fee or token transfer; the only economic cost is the EVM gas to send / requestReveal. Who-pays-whom: sender pays gas to send + store ciphertext; the reveal-triggerer (anyone, for timed) pays the requestReveal gas.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect EVM wallet → ensure Neo X Mainnet → Compose: pick recipient (0x address), body (≤2000 chars), and delivery mode. Recipient-only: encrypt to oracle key, sendMessage(recipient, ciphertext, unlockTime=0) → recipient later opens Inbox, signs the reveal statement, oracle returns plaintext, shown locally + cached on-device (never written on-chain). Time-locked: pick a future reveal datetime, sendMessage(…, unlockTime>0) → message shows Locked until the time, then Ready → anyone triggers requestReveal → relayer posts plaintext on-chain (now public to all) → row flips to Revealed. Inbox/outbox reconstructed from inboxOf/outboxOf id lists + getMessage. No funds lifecycle; exit = nothing to recover (no value escrowed).

gaps.title: Time-locked mode does not warn that the plaintext becomes PUBLIC on-chain before the user commits
gaps.evidence: The mode toggle hint reads only 'Revealed publicly on-chain at a set time' (messages.ts:25 modeTimedHint) and the pre-send note 'After it, anyone can trigger the reveal and the oracle posts the plaintext on-chain for everyone' (messages.ts:31-34 timedNote) sits below the fold of the compose card (PlayArea.tsx:239). A first-time user reading 'Encrypted & time-locked messages' (heroTitle) and choosing 'Time-locked' can reasonably believe the message stays encrypted-to-recipient and merely auto-opens for the recipient at the set time — not that the cleartext is written on-chain for the entire world. This is the inverse privacy guarantee of the recipient-only mode sitting right next to it.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: when lockMode==='timed', render a prominent warning chip/callout directly on the Time-locked toggle option and adjacent to the reveal-date picker (not just the small note) — e.g. 'Public reveal: after the unlock time the message body is posted on-chain in cleartext, readable by anyone.' Add an explicit confirm affordance (checkbox or a distinct button label like 'Schedule public reveal') so the user acknowledges the publicness before sendMessage.

gaps.title: Recipient-only decryption is device-local cache only; copy implies portable/durable readability
gaps.evidence: After a recipient reveals, plaintext is shown and persisted only via on-device cache keyed by contract:id:recipient (main.tsx:49-68,288-293) and overlaid on refresh (overlayCachedPlaintext, main.tsx:137-146). On a different device or after clearing storage the user must re-sign + re-call the oracle to read again. The UI never states this — modeRecipientHint says 'Only the recipient can ever decrypt it' (messages.ts:23) with no mention that the readable plaintext is not stored, only the right-to-decrypt. A recipient may assume the decrypted text is durably theirs.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: after a successful recipient reveal, add a one-line note on the message row (e.g. 'Decrypted on this device. Re-open with your wallet to read again elsewhere.') so the recipient understands the message is re-derivable via signature, not stored as readable text.

apps.business_model: Manifest frames this as 'Confidential Transfer' / DeFi (neo-manifest.json: category defi, permissions invoke:primary + payments, tags privacy/transfer/payments) — a private Neo N3 payment product where recipient, amount and memo are hidden via Morpheus TEE rather than on-chain zk. The implied user = someone who wants to actually move GAS/NEO privately to a recipient. The economic promise is a settled private transfer ('How a confidential transfer settles' with steps Deposit → Local encryption → TEE validation → Release or refund, appConfig.ts:185-205). BUT the deployed reality has NO contract (contracts:{}), no token movement, and no settlement: the app only encrypts the {recipient, amount, memo} JSON to the Morpheus oracle key and POSTs the ciphertext to a confidential-store, returning a secretRef + note_commitment + nullifier (PlayArea.tsx:275-380). Nothing is deposited, escrowed, or released; no value ever leaves the user's wallet. The real product is a 'seal a private transfer intent' demo, not a payment.
apps.intended_workflow: As implied by copy: (1) deposit/lock asset or sign a payment intent, (2) seal the private fields locally, (3) Morpheus TEE decrypts + checks nullifier reuse + signs a settlement envelope, (4) user submits the returned settlement intent through the wallet to release-or-refund the funds. As actually built: pick network (testnet/mainnet, badged live/degraded) → pick asset (GAS/NEO) → enter recipient + amount + memo → 'Seal private transfer' fetches the oracle public key, encrypts the payload, stores ciphertext → shows secretRef/commitment/nullifier with copy buttons and a device-local history list. There is no deposit step, no settlement-intent retrieval, no submit-to-wallet step, and no release/refund — the workflow dead-ends at the three opaque hashes.

gaps.title: Product promises a private money transfer; the app never moves (or escrows) any funds
gaps.evidence: Hero/manifest sell a transfer that settles: heroTitle 'Confidential transfer desk', heroBody 'Seal recipient, amount, memo… then Morpheus runs the private compute path' (appConfig.ts:83-87), manifest permissions.payments:true and the 4-step 'How a confidential transfer settles' incl. 'Deposit or wallet intent' and 'Release or refund' (appConfig.ts:185-205). Yet sealTransfer only encrypts JSON and POSTs to /api/morpheus/confidential/store (PlayArea.tsx:309-357); there is no contract (neo-manifest.json contracts:{}), no NEP-17 transfer, no wallet invoke. The user's amount/recipient are sealed but the recipient never receives anything. A first-timer entering '5 GAS' to an address reasonably expects 5 GAS to be sent privately — it is not.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only reframing: change hero + button + status copy from a transfer that 'settles' to what actually happens — 'Seal a private transfer intent for Morpheus confidential compute.' Rename the CTA result so the user knows the output is a sealed intent reference, not a sent payment. Add an explicit 'No funds were moved — this seals an encrypted intent' banner above the seal button (today that disclosure only appears inside the error state via safeCopy, PlayArea.tsx:586). If a real settlement lane is intended, it cannot be built (no contract, frozen) — so the honest fix is to stop framing it as a completed transfer.

gaps.title: Lifecycle is truncated: steps 1 (Deposit) and 4 (Release/refund) are described but have no UI
gaps.evidence: The steps explainer renders all four stages incl. step1 'Deposit or wallet intent' and step4 'Release or refund — The user submits the returned settlement intent through the wallet' (appConfig.ts:186-205, rendered PlayArea.tsx:722-745). But the app exposes only the seal action; there is no deposit affordance, no 'fetch settlement envelope', and no 'submit settlement intent' button. The sealed-intents history (PlayArea.tsx:633-720) lets the user copy secretRef/commitment but offers no next action — the commitment/nullifier are dead-ends with no redeem/settle/cancel path.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: either (a) demote steps 1 and 4 to clearly-labeled 'not available in this app' / 'handled by your wallet & the settlement service' so the user isn't told to 'submit the returned settlement intent' through a button that doesn't exist, or (b) if a settlement endpoint exists, add a 'Check settlement status' / 'Retrieve settlement envelope' action against the stored secretRef so the sealed intent has a real downstream step instead of dead-ending.

gaps.title: secretRef / commitment / nullifier are surfaced with no explanation of what the user does with them
gaps.evidence: On success the app shows three cryptographic identifiers — Secret ref, Commitment, Nullifier — each with a copy button (PlayArea.tsx:594-628) and persists them in history. The labels (resultSecretRef/resultCommitment/resultNullifier, appConfig.ts:161-163) are not explained; statusStored says only 'Ciphertext stored. Morpheus confidential compute can now decrypt…' (appConfig.ts:125-128). A user cannot tell whether they must keep these, share them with the recipient, or hand them to a relayer to complete the transfer. The value delivered ('I sealed an intent') is illegible.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: under the results add a one-line purpose for each field (e.g. 'Secret ref — keep this to retrieve/settle the intent later', 'Commitment — public anchor a verifier can check', 'Nullifier — prevents double-spend of this intent') and a sentence on who needs them next. Tie this to the lifecycle fix so the user knows the concrete next move.

apps.business_model: A free identity tooling app (manifest category tools; permissions read:blockchain + wallet:sign-message; no payments). User = a developer/relying-party/wallet owner who needs a portable identity credential. Value: resolve a live Morpheus NeoDID document via the resolver API, assemble a canonical 'passport' credential payload (subject DID, claim, audience, DID-document metadata, sha256 digest), and OPTIONALLY bind it to the connected wallet via an off-chain personal-sign (no transaction broadcast). The credential is then copied/handed to another miniapp or relying party. Economic model: none — purely a credential workbench; the wallet 'proof' is a signature, not a payment, and explicitly does not broadcast (appConfig.ts:105-108 walletProofHint, feature3Desc).
apps.intended_workflow: Enter Subject DID (did:morpheus:neo_n3:…), pick proof provider (wallet | github | email), set claim + audience → 'Resolve and Build' calls the NeoDID resolver, builds the payload, computes the digest, shows the JSON + summary (version, service count, digest) → for the wallet provider, 'Sign Passport' signs the canonical payload off-chain and attaches signature/publicKey/address (proof.status prepared→signed) → 'Copy Payload' to hand off. github/email providers only PREPARE an unsigned attestation package and route the user to external attestation docs (PlayArea.tsx:60-67,193-206). Degraded-runtime warning shown when versionId==='unversioned' (missing TEE verification key). No funds, no on-chain state, nothing to recover.

gaps.title: Hero does not state the credential is off-chain / non-broadcasting, so users may expect on-chain registration
gaps.evidence: The panel title/desc 'NeoDID Passport Builder … optionally bind it to the connected wallet signature' (appConfig.ts:54-58) reads like an identity registration. The crucial fact that signing does NOT broadcast a transaction and the passport is just a portable JSON handed to a relying party is only in the per-provider hint (walletProofHint, appConfig.ts:105-108) and the empty-state copy, not in the hero. A newcomer might 'Sign Passport' expecting their DID to be registered/anchored on-chain.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: add a one-line subtitle or chip in the hero, e.g. 'Builds a portable credential and an off-chain wallet proof — nothing is broadcast on-chain.' This makes the no-transaction, hand-off-to-relying-party mental model legible up front.

apps.business_model: A read-first security console for Neo N3 AA (abstract account) social recovery, targeting an account owner / backup-owner / recovery operator (manifest category console/utility; permissions aa; no payments). Backed by the live AA core (UnifiedSmartWalletV3) + the MorpheusSocialRecoveryVerifier (0x198b3a9c…). Value: given an account locator, read the on-chain recovery binding — bound verifier, backup owner, recovery (escape) timelock in seconds, escape active/triggered status — so an operator can sanity-check recovery posture BEFORE attempting an ownership change; then PREPARE guardrailed deep links (recovery preview + recovery credential) into the live AA identity workspace where the actual on-chain recovery is executed. No funds move here and no recovery transaction is signed in-app; the economic stake is the account's custody itself (control of the wallet), which is why the UI fails-closed on link generation.
apps.intended_workflow: Enter account address/Hash160 → Query State reads getVerifier/getBackupOwner/getEscapeTimelock/isEscapeActive/getEscapeTriggeredAt from the AA core (main.tsx:239-337) and renders verifier (or 'Not configured'), backup owner, timelock seconds, escape status → operator reviews recovery posture → fills new owner + expiry (5–1440 min) + optional verifier override (badged match/mismatch vs the bound verifier) + optional template id → Prepare: Open/Copy/Share the recovery-preview and recovery-credential links (built against the AA identity workspace, main.tsx:136-202) → the operator (or a guardian) opens those links in the AA workspace to perform the actual on-chain recovery execution. Exit/custody recovery is completed off-app in the AA workspace, not here.

gaps.title: Manifest/README promise 'final recovery execution' but the app only reads state and prepares hand-off links
gaps.evidence: neo-manifest.json description: 'Operator surface for AA guardian policy, recovery ticket flow, timelock review, and final recovery execution.' README.md (line 3): '…timelock review, and final recovery execution.' But there is no in-app execution: the only on-chain action is the read-only queryGuardianState; recovery is delegated via deep links to the AA identity workspace (main.tsx:136-202,387-394) and the in-app step3 copy itself says 'The AA identity and app workspaces handle the on-chain recovery execution' (messages.ts:179-180). So the top-line product description over-promises 'final recovery execution' that the app deliberately does not do.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: the in-app copy is already honest ('read-first console', 'AA workspaces handle execution'); align the outward promise to it — the gap is the manifest description/README wording. Since the manifest description surfaces in listings, reword it to 'Read-first recovery console: inspect guardian/verifier/timelock state and prepare guarded recovery links — execution happens in the AA workspace.' (manifest is a config/frontend file, editable.)

gaps.title: Hand-off to the AA workspace is not framed as 'where you actually recover', so the link buttons look like the end of the flow
gaps.evidence: The flow strip ends at '03 Share credential' (PlayArea.tsx:211-215) and the prepared preview/credential URLs render as raw strings at the bottom (PlayArea.tsx:393-408). The decisive next step — opening the link in the AA identity workspace to sign the actual recovery — is only implied by the secondary 'Open Identity Workspace' / 'Open AA Workspace' buttons in the side rail (PlayArea.tsx:374-389), which read as generic nav rather than 'continue your recovery here'. A first-time operator who copies the link may not realize the recovery is finished elsewhere.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: relabel/annotate the flow so step 03 explicitly says the link continues in the AA workspace, and add a short note next to the prepared links like 'Open this link in the AA identity workspace to sign the recovery — it is not executed here.' Optionally promote the 'Open Identity Workspace' button to a primary 'Continue recovery in AA workspace' affordance once links are prepared.

apps.business_model: A free (gas-only) credentialing platform on Neo N3 backed by the dedicated MiniAppSoulboundCertificate NEP-11 contract (0x4e920c7f…). Two user roles: ISSUER (an academy/org/event organizer) who creates reusable templates (name, issuerName, category, maxSupply, description) and mints non-transferable certificates to recipient wallets with recipientName/achievement/memo; and VERIFIER/RECIPIENT (any counterparty) who looks up a certificate by token id to confirm owner, achievement, issue time, and revocation status. The certificates are soulbound — the contract's NEP-11 transfer is gated so they cannot move between wallets — making them trustworthy identity/achievement attestations. Economic model: no protocol fee or payment (contract has no OnNEP17Payment, no fee param); the only cost is the issuer's gas to createTemplate/issueCertificate/revoke. Who-pays-whom: issuer pays gas to mint and to revoke; verification is a free read. Issuer authority is enforced on-chain (issueCertificate/revokeCertificate assert the issuer witness + template ownership).
apps.intended_workflow: Issuer connects wallet → Create Template (issuer/category/supply cap/description) signed on-chain → Issue Certificate: pick an active template + recipient address + recipientName + achievement + memo → issueCertificate mints a soulbound NEP-11 token id '<templateId>-<serial>' to the recipient (auto-verified after issue) → issuer can Activate/Deactivate templates and Copy an issuing-shortcut link (issuer-only) → Recipient/verifier: enter or open a verify deep-link (?verifyTokenId=…) to look up the certificate; the detail card shows recipient/achievement/owner/issue time + a token-id QR + Copy/Share verify link → only the issuing wallet sees the Revoke action (verifiedIsIssuer gate, useSoulbound.ts:611-630) which calls revokeCertificate, flipping status to Revoked with a timestamp. Lifecycle states (active/inactive template, valid/revoked certificate, sold-out) are all surfaced. No funds to recover; certificates are permanent unless revoked.

gaps.title: The defining 'soulbound / non-transferable' value prop is buried in a form helper, not asserted in the hero
