gaps.evidence: The single most important property — these certificates CANNOT be transferred/sold, which is the whole reason they are trustworthy — appears only in the Issue panel helper 'Mint a non-transferable NEP-11 certificate…' (issueHelp, messages.ts:58-61) and in the docs features list (feature1 'Non-transferable', messages.ts:140-141). The hero shows title + 'Issuer workspace' eyebrow + docSubtitle 'On-chain, non-transferable NEP-11 certificates' (PlayArea.tsx:226-244) — the docSubtitle does mention it, but a verifier landing via a ?verifyTokenId deep link sees no statement that what they're verifying is tamper-/transfer-proof. The trust guarantee a verifier most needs is not emphasized at the point of verification.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy: in the Verify detail card add a small reassurance line/badge such as 'Soulbound — this certificate is bound to the owner wallet and cannot be transferred', so a verifier opening a shared link immediately understands why the credential is trustworthy. The data to back it (it is a soulbound NEP-11) is already true on-chain; this just surfaces it where trust is decided.

apps.business_model: An organizer-side NEP-11 event-ticketing registry on a self-contained Neo N3 contract (0x90bad472…, supportedstandards NEP-11). The user is an EVENT ORGANIZER (the connected wallet, gated by Runtime.CheckWitness(creator)). They publish event metadata on-chain (createEvent: name/venue/start/end/maxSupply/notes), then ISSUE tickets one-by-one to specific attendee addresses (issueTicket(creator,recipient,eventId,seat,memo) → mints a real NEP-11 token id '<eventId>-<serial>'), and validate attendees at the door (checkIn marks used). Economics: there is NO sale, price, or payment anywhere in the ABI — createEvent/issueTicket take no GAS, tickets are minted FREE to recipients the organizer chooses. So the true model is a comp/invite/allowlist ticketing & door-control system (think conference badges, RSVP passes, guest lists), not a paid box office. Value: tamper-proof on-chain attendee list + cryptographic door check-in + transferable (giftable) NEP-11 passes. Who pays whom: nobody pays anyone on-chain; the organizer pays only Neo network/system fees to write events/tickets.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Organizer connects wallet (also acts as refresh). 2) Create Event (name, venue, schedule, max ticket supply, notes) → EventCreated, event becomes Active. 3) Issue Ticket to each attendee's Neo address with optional seat/zone + memo → TicketIssued mints a NEP-11 token id; minted count increments toward maxSupply (soldOut = supply exhausted, not money). 4) Attendee opens 'My Tickets', sees the pass with seat + a token-id QR, and may transfer/gift an unused ticket to another wallet. 5) At the door the organizer opens Check-in, scans/pastes the token id, Lookup shows seat/owner/Valid-or-Used, then Check-in marks it Used on-chain (TicketCheckedIn). 6) Organizer can Deactivate/Activate an event to open/close further issuance. State lifecycle: event Active⇄Inactive; ticket Valid→Used (one-way) or transferred to a new owner while still Valid. No funds ever held, so there is no refund/withdraw path needed — exit is simply that tickets are NEP-11 assets the holder keeps or transfers.

gaps.title: Copy implies a paid 'sales' box office that does not exist on-chain
gaps.evidence: emptyEventsHint (apps/event-ticket-pass/src/locale/messages.ts:42) tells the organizer the workflow is to 'issue attendee tickets, pause sales, and check people in.' There is no sales/price/payment in the ABI — createEvent and issueTicket take no GAS amount (contracts/build/MiniAppEventTicketPass.manifest.json: createEvent params are name/venue/times/maxSupply/notes; issueTicket is creator/recipient/eventId/seat/memo). 'soldOut' (messages.ts:51) is shown when minted >= maxSupply (useEventTicket.ts:511, PlayArea.tsx:229) — i.e. supply exhaustion, not a sale. A first-time organizer reads 'pause sales' and expects attendees to buy tickets and money to flow; in reality the organizer hand-issues every ticket free to addresses they type in.
gaps.fix: Reframe copy from a box-office model to an invite/allowlist model. Change emptyEventsHint to '…issue passes to attendee addresses, pause issuance, and check people in at the door.' Rename the 'Sold out'/soldOut string to a supply word ('Supply reached' / 'All passes issued') and consider an explicit 'Free passes — issued to addresses you choose. No payment is taken on-chain.' note in the Create or Issue panel so the absence of a buy flow is intentional, not a missing feature. Frontend-only copy change.

gaps.title: On-chain truth (real NEP-11 token, tx) is not externally verifiable from the UI
gaps.evidence: The whole value prop is 'tickets are real on-chain NEP-11 tokens' (docDescription messages.ts:115-117) and the evidence panel shows the txid (latestResult includes txid, useEventTicket.ts:478,549). But the txid and token id are rendered as plain text only (PlayArea.tsx evidence section ~511-529; ticket-pass__id code at 423-434) — there is no link to a Neo explorer to confirm the mint/check-in actually happened, nor a way for an attendee to prove their pass is genuine to anyone outside the app.
gaps.fix: Make the issue/check-in txid and the ticket token id click-through to a Neo N3 explorer (build the URL frontend-side from the active network, as evm-chain.ts already does for Neo X). On the ticket card and in the evidence panel, render txid/tokenId as a link 'View on explorer' so organizer and attendee can independently verify the on-chain mint, owner, and check-in. Frontend-only.

apps.business_model: A free, dependency-free SHA-256 timestamping/notary tool (manifest contracts:{}, transactions:false). The user is anyone who wants to prove a document/text existed and was hashed at a point in time. Core model is a DEVICE-LOCAL proof journal: content is hashed in-browser (crypto.subtle), stored in local cache with an incrementing id + timestamp (useTimestampProof.ts:137-185), never uploaded. The optional paid/on-chain layer is an 'anchor': a 0-GAS GAS.transfer self→self with data 'timestamp-proof:<digest>' (anchorProof, lines 194-250), which writes the digest into a real, lookup-able Neo transaction so a third party can later confirm the digest+time existed on-chain. Economics: local proofs are free; anchoring costs only Neo network/system fees (no app fee, no custody). Value: provenance/notarization without trusting any server; anchored proofs become independently verifiable.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Paste text or a document hash → Create Proof: hashed locally, saved to the device journal with id/timestamp, marked 'Local only'. 2) Optionally connect a wallet and Anchor on-chain → a 0-GAS self-transfer embeds the digest; proof flips to 'Anchored on-chain' and stores the real anchor txid. 3) Anytime, Verify by proof id, SHA-256 digest, or original content → shows id, timestamp, digest, anchor status, and (if anchored) the anchor txid. 4) Copy digest or a self-describing JSON 'reference' to share. State lifecycle: Local only → Anchored on-chain (one-way); proofs can be deleted/cleared locally. No funds held, so no refund path — exit is keeping/sharing the digest or the on-chain tx reference.

gaps.title: The promised third-party on-chain verification is not reachable — anchor txid is dead text, no explorer link, no re-verify
gaps.evidence: The product's reason to anchor is 'so a third party can verify the digest and time on-chain' (docDescription messages.ts:62-63; step3 line 67). But the anchor txid is rendered only as a static mono string (PlayArea.tsx:144-149) with no link to a Neo explorer, and there is no affordance to re-fetch/confirm the on-chain tx or its data field. Verify (verifyProof, useTimestampProof.ts:279-303) only matches against THIS device's local journal (findProof reads readStoredProofs, lines 252-277) — so on a fresh device or for a third party, 'Verify' cannot confirm an anchored proof at all. The headline trust claim is undeliverable from the UI.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: make the anchor txid a click-through link to a Neo N3 explorer tx page (build URL from active network like evm-chain.ts does). Add a 'How to verify' note explaining that anyone can open the tx and read 'timestamp-proof:<digest>' in the data/witness field, and that the block time is the proof time. Optionally add an on-chain lookup path in Verify that, given a txid (or the pasted JSON reference's anchorTxid), reads the transaction via the existing chain/RPC and confirms the embedded digest — turning Verify into something a third party can actually use, not just a local-journal lookup.

gaps.title: Anchoring's economic cost and what it buys are not surfaced before the user commits
gaps.evidence: Anchor sends a real transaction that costs Neo network/system fees, but the only fee hint is the 'Connect a wallet to anchor on-chain' string (messages.ts:29); neither the anchor button nor surrounding copy states that anchoring costs gas or precisely what anchoring adds over a local proof (public, permanent, third-party-verifiable). The localOnly vs anchoredOnChain badges (PlayArea.tsx:139-141) describe the state but not the trade-off the user is choosing.
gaps.fix: Add a one-line note near the Anchor button: 'Anchoring writes the digest into a public Neo transaction (small network fee). Local proofs stay private and free.' Frontend-only copy.

apps.business_model: A free wallet utility (manifest contracts:{}) for cryptographic message/file attestation. The user signs a message (or a locally-hashed file digest) with their Neo wallet to produce a portable signature proof — or broadcasts the message on-chain as a 0-GAS self-transfer with the text in the data field for public, permanent evidence. Economics: off-chain Sign is free (no gas); Broadcast pays normal Neo network+system fees (~0.01–0.05 GAS, disclosed in networkFeeNote messages.ts:82-85). No custody, no app fee; the wallet holds the key (chain.signMessage), the app never touches it. Value: prove authorship/consent off-chain, or anchor a public statement on-chain.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Write a message (or Hash & load a file → 'sha256:<digest>' is loaded, file never leaves device, useSignAnything.ts:169-192). 2a) Sign Message → wallet returns signature (+ public key when available) for off-chain verification; or 2b) Broadcast Message → 0-GAS GAS.transfer self→self with the message as data (lines 115-161), returning a real txid (or a pending flag if none yet). 3) Copy the signature or the tx hash as proof. Signing and broadcasting coexist for the same message; changing the message clears both (syncResultMessage, lines 56-64). Byte cap 1024 enforced for broadcast. No state held server-side; exit is taking the signature/txid elsewhere.

gaps.title: Copy promises off-chain verification ('use in any verifier') but the app offers no verify affordance or guidance
gaps.evidence: verifyText/docFeature4Desc (messages.ts:120-124, 185-189) tell the user to 'Use your Neo address, the message, and the signature in any verifier to prove authorship', and the app deliberately captures the public key alongside the signature for exactly this (useSignAnything.ts:36-38, 90-93). But the UI only emits the signature + pubkey; there is no in-app verify step and no concrete pointer to a verifier, so the attestation lifecycle (produce → verify) is half-built from the user's perspective.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: either add a small 'Verify a signature' panel that takes address+message+signature and checks it client-side, or at minimum surface the exact triplet to copy as one bundle (address, message, signature, publicKey) and link to a known Neo signature verifier so the promised verify step is actionable.

gaps.title: Broadcast tx hash is not linked to an explorer
gaps.evidence: Broadcast's whole point is 'public on-chain evidence' (signHeroSubtitle messages.ts:13-16; broadcastText 116-119), and the txid is shown/copyable (PlayArea.tsx:199-209) — but only as a truncated string with a copy button, no explorer link to confirm the transaction and its embedded message actually landed.
gaps.fix: Render the broadcast tx hash as a click-through link to a Neo N3 explorer (URL built from the active network), so the user can immediately confirm the public record. Frontend-only.

apps.business_model: A free, fully client-side developer/cold-storage toolkit (manifest contracts:{}, transactions:false, permissions only read:blockchain). The user is a developer or self-custody holder who needs to generate a Neo N3 account offline, convert between key formats (WIF ⇄ private key ⇄ public key ⇄ address/script hash), and disassemble NeoVM script hex into readable opcodes. Economics: none — no fees, no on-chain writes; all crypto runs on-device (useNeoConvert.ts header; generateAccount, useConverter.ts:76-143). Optional: if a wallet is connected it shows live NEO/GAS balances (read-only). Value: safe key handling without trusting a server, plus a QR-backed paper-wallet PDF for cold storage.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Generate New Account → address/pubkey/privkey/WIF created locally; secrets masked by default, reveal toggle, then Download Paper Wallet (PDF, gated on reveal — downloadPaperWallet throws if no account, useNeoConvert.ts:270-288). 2) Convert Key → paste WIF/private/public key, Neo N3 address, or NeoVM script hex; auto-detected and converted, deriving address/pubkey/WIF/script hashes or a disassembled opcode list (useConverter.ts:76-143). 3) Copy any field; sensitive fields stay masked until revealed. Optionally connect a wallet to view balances. No funds held, no on-chain state, no lifecycle beyond local generate/convert; exit is copying/saving the derived material.

gaps.title: On-device / no-network security promise is stated but the wallet-balance read (which does hit the network) isn't distinguished
gaps.evidence: Copy repeatedly promises everything runs on-device with nothing sent over the network (onDeviceNote messages.ts:296-298; heroSubtitle; docDescription 'no server calls'). That is true for key generation/conversion, but connecting a wallet to show NEO/GAS balances performs read:blockchain RPC calls (useNeoConvert.ts:130-146, loadBalances). A security-minded cold-storage user could read 'nothing is ever sent over the network' as absolute and be surprised the balance feature talks to a node.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only copy nuance: scope the on-device claim to key generation/conversion ('Key generation and conversion run entirely on your device — keys are never transmitted'), and note that the optional balance view makes read-only RPC calls when a wallet is connected. Keeps the strong, accurate guarantee for the sensitive path.

apps.business_model: A self-custodial, on-chain time-lock vault for personal/sentimental messages. The user (a wallet owner who wants to commit to a future self, send a dated gift, or seal a secret) locks a 0.2 GAS REFUNDABLE DEPOSIT plus the SHA-256 hash of a message for 1-3650 days via MiniAppTimeCapsule (testnet/mainnet 0x3e88058e..., verified ABI: bury/reveal/withdraw/getCapsule/creditOf). The full message + title stay ON-DEVICE; only the hash + lock are on-chain. reveal() after the unlock time returns the deposit atomically — so the economic model is escrow, not a fee: money in == money out for the owner. A second revenue lane is 'fishing': any other user can pay a 0.05 GAS discovery fee on a PUBLIC, unrevealed capsule, and the contract forwards that fee on-chain to the capsule's owner as a tip (Fished event). Who-pays-whom: owner deposits to self (refundable); fisher tips owner (0.05 GAS, non-refundable). Recovery path: withdraw(account) returns unused prepaid credit if a bury failed after deposit.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet. 2) Write title + secret message, set lock days (1-3650), choose Personal/Gift/Memorial/Announcement/Secret, toggle public/private. 3) Confirm — wallet transfers 0.2 GAS deposit (memo miniapp-timecapsule:bury) then bury() consumes it as the locked amount; title/content saved on-device under the new capsule id. 4) Capsule sits LOCKED until unlock date (badge: Locked). 5) On/after unlock date the owner taps Open → reveal() returns the 0.2 GAS deposit + surfaces the on-device message (badge: Revealed). 6) Optional: tip another user by Fishing their public unrevealed capsule for 0.05 GAS. 7) Recovery: if a deposit landed but bury failed, a Reusable Deposit Credit banner offers withdraw() back to wallet.

gaps.title: Fishing's value to the fisher is overpromised — 'discover' delivers nothing
gaps.evidence: locale/messages.ts:58-62 frames fishing as 'Fish (0.05 GAS tip)' / 'Pay 0.05 GAS to discover another user's public, unrevealed capsule.' But in useTimeCapsule.ts fishCapsule() (lines 728-773) the contract only marks the capsule fished and forwards the fee to the owner as a tip; the fisher receives NOTHING back — no content (the message is on the owner's device + the capsule stays locked/unrevealed), no ownership, no read. fishResult (messages.ts:63) just says 'Fished capsule {id}'. A first-time user reads 'discover' as 'I get to see/claim it' and pays 0.05 GAS expecting a payoff that never comes.
gaps.fix: Reframe the fishing copy as what it actually is: a tip/support action, not a reveal. Change fishButton/fishDescription/fishResult to make clear the fisher is sending an on-chain tip to encourage a stranger's public capsule and gets back only a public acknowledgement (capsule id + that it exists), not the content. e.g. fishDescription: 'Send a 0.05 GAS tip to the owner of a random public, unrevealed capsule. You are cheering them on — the message stays sealed until its owner reveals it.' Frontend-only copy change in locale/messages.ts.

gaps.title: Fisher cannot choose which capsule to tip — auto-picks newest, no preview
gaps.evidence: fishCapsule() (useTimeCapsule.ts:728-739) calls loadPublicCandidates() and unconditionally takes candidates[0] (newest other-owner public capsule). The PlayArea (PlayArea.tsx:171-186) renders a single 'Fish' button with no candidate list, so the user cannot see the pool of fishable capsules, their categories/unlock dates, or pick a target before paying. The product implies cross-user discovery but the UI is a blind one-shot.
gaps.fix: Surface loadPublicCandidates() as a small browsable list (id, category badge, unlock date) above the Fish button so the user picks a target; pass the chosen id into fishCapsule. The candidates are already fetched on-chain; this is a frontend-only affordance over existing reads.

apps.business_model: A hacker-bounty challenge market on the deployed MiniAppUnbreakableVault (testnet 0x78fbd57c..., mainnet 0x198bfccc..., verified ABI v2.0.0). Two roles: a CREATOR locks a GAS bounty (min 1 GAS) behind a SHA-256 secret hash at a chosen difficulty (Easy/Medium/Hard); CHALLENGERS pay a difficulty-tiered attempt fee (0.1/0.5/1 GAS, confirmed via getVaultConstants attemptFeeEasy/Medium/Hard) to submit a secret guess. Economic engine (confirmed on-chain): every FAILED attempt fee folds INTO the bounty (vault #1: created at 1 GAS, after 1 Easy attempt bounty=1.1 GAS), so the prize grows. A correct secret pays the bounty to the winner ATOMICALLY MINUS a 2% platform fee (platformFeeBps=200, confirmed). Vaults expire after 30 days (defaultExpirySeconds=2592000); an unbroken expired vault is reclaimable by the creator (claimExpiredVault → VaultExpired refund). Anyone may top up an active bounty (increaseBounty). Who-pays-whom: challengers pay attempt fees that accrue to the pot + platform; winner takes pot−2%; creator reclaims on expiry.
apps.intended_workflow: CREATE: connect wallet → set title, optional public hint, bounty (≥1 GAS), difficulty, secret (entered twice to avoid lock-out) → confirm → deposit GAS (memo miniapp-unbreakablevault:create) + createVault → share the Vault ID publicly. BREAK: load a vault by ID → read title/hint/bounty/difficulty/attempt-fee/attempts/days-left → pay the tiered attempt fee + submit secret guess → AttemptMade event resolves success/fail; correct secret pays bounty−2% atomically (VaultBroken). GROW: anyone adds to an active bounty (increaseBounty). EXIT: creator of an expired, unbroken vault reclaims the escrowed bounty (claimExpiredVault).

gaps.title: The 2% platform fee on the winning payout is never surfaced at the point of decision
gaps.evidence: The deployed contract takes platformFeeBps=200 (2%) off the bounty on a win (confirmed via getVaultConstants; VaultBroken(vaultId,winner,reward) pays reward=bounty−2%). The only mention is docDescription (locale/messages.ts:97-100) 'Winners receive the bounty minus a 2% platform fee' buried in docs. The interactive break panel (PlayArea.tsx:285-288) shows the gross bounty as detail-value--accent with NO net-of-fee figure, and the create form never tells the creator 2% of their posted bounty goes to the platform on a win. A challenger weighing a 1 GAS attempt fee against a displayed 5 GAS bounty is actually playing for 4.9 GAS.
gaps.fix: In the break panel, add a derived 'You win: {bounty × 0.98} GAS (after 2% fee)' row beside the gross bounty (baseUnitsToGas already exists; the 2% is a constant from getVaultConstants, already readable). In the create form, add one line: 'On a successful break, a 2% platform fee is deducted from the bounty.' Frontend-only — both numbers are already on-chain.

gaps.title: The bounty-growth mechanic (failed fees grow the prize) is invisible in the live UI
gaps.evidence: This is the app's core hook (feature2Name 'Bounty Growth', and confirmed on-chain: attempt fees fold into the bounty — vault #1 grew 1→1.1 GAS after one attempt). But the break panel (PlayArea.tsx:285-302) shows bounty + attempt-fee + attempt-count as three flat rows with no statement that the current bounty already INCLUDES prior failed fees or that the user's own fee will grow it if they miss. attemptCostNote (messages.ts:43-46) mentions 'grows the bounty' but only appears under the attempt button, not tied to the bounty figure a challenger evaluates first.
gaps.fix: Add a one-line annotation under the bounty row: 'Each failed attempt adds its fee to this bounty — it grows as more people try.' This connects the displayed bounty to the live attemptCount the panel already shows. Frontend copy only.

gaps.title: Difficulty selector shows the fee but doesn't say who pays it (challenger, not creator)
gaps.evidence: The create form difficulty dropdown (PlayArea.tsx:212-216) renders 'Easy · 0.1 GAS', 'Medium · 0.5 GAS', 'Hard · 1 GAS'. A first-time creator can reasonably read this as a fee THEY pay to create at that difficulty, when in fact it is the per-attempt fee CHALLENGERS will pay (and that the creator only pays the bounty). feature3Desc 'Attempt fees scale with difficulty' is in docs, not next to the selector.
gaps.fix: Relabel the difficulty field or add a hint under it: 'Difficulty sets the per-attempt fee challengers pay (Easy 0.1 / Medium 0.5 / Hard 1 GAS). You only fund the bounty.' Frontend copy only.

apps.business_model: A paid 'right-to-forget' / commitment ritual on MiniAppGraveyard (testnet 0xb55aa635...). The user anchors the SHA-256 hash of a memory (Secret/Regret/Wish/Confession/Other) on-chain for a small burial fee (0.1 GAS, read live from getPlatformStats.buryFee), keeping the plaintext on-device. They can later attach a free epitaph (addEpitaph, no deposit) or pay a 10× 'forgetting fee' (1 GAS, getPlatformStats.forgetFee) to mark it Forgotten — which does NOT delete the record, only appends a paid 'forgotten' state to the permanent audit trail. Economic model: prepaid-GAS — deposits (memo miniapp-graveyard:memory) credit the caller, then buryMemory/forgetMemory consume it. Both fees are spent (not refundable). Who-pays-whom: user → contract (fees are sunk, no payout/reclaim). Value is symbolic: a permanent, inspectable, hash-committed record of having buried (and optionally renounced) a memory.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet. 2) Write a memory (hashed locally → only hash on-chain) OR paste a pre-made hash; pick a record tag. 3) Review panel shows hash quality, target preview, wallet action, and the 0.1 GAS burial fee. 4) Confirm (two-step: Review → Bury) → deposit 0.1 GAS + buryMemory → MemoryBuried; row appears in Burial Records. 5) Optionally add a free epitaph. 6) Optionally Forget: a two-tap confirm surfaces the 1 GAS forgetting fee before paying → forgetMemory → row flips to Forgotten, still listed. There is no money-out: burial and forget fees are sunk by design.

gaps.title: Where the fees go (sunk, no payout/refund) is never stated — user may expect to reclaim
gaps.evidence: Burial fee (0.1 GAS) and forgetting fee (1 GAS) are non-refundable sinks — the contract has no withdraw/reclaim path and no payout to anyone (verified: only buryMemory/forgetMemory/addEpitaph mutate, all consume prepaid GAS). Yet the hero stat is labelled 'Burial Fees (est.)' with a '~' value (PlayArea.tsx:86-89, messages.ts:157) which reads like a reclaimable/tracked balance, and no copy states the fees are spent forever. The warning text (messages.ts:32-35) covers permanence of the record but not the irreversibility of the spend.
gaps.fix: Add one line to the burial review panel and the forget confirm: 'This fee is spent (not refundable) — it pays for the permanent on-chain record.' Optionally rename the hero metric from the ambiguous 'Burial Fees (est.)' to 'GAS spent on burials (est.)'. Frontend copy only.

gaps.title: The 10× forget fee vs. burial fee is not justified — 'forget' value prop is muddy
gaps.evidence: Burying costs 0.1 GAS; forgetting costs 1 GAS (10×, confirmed forgetFee default + live read). The locale honestly says forgetting 'records a paid state change on-chain and cannot be reversed' and 'does not delete the audit trail' (messages.ts:129-132, 161-163). But a newcomer reasonably asks 'why pay 10× to mark something forgotten when it stays visible forever?' — the product never frames the emotional/ritual payoff (renunciation, closure) that makes paying MORE to forget than to bury make sense.
gaps.fix: Add a short framing line near the Forget control, e.g. 'Forgetting is a deliberate, paid act of letting go — the record stays as proof you chose to release it.' Frontend copy only; turns a confusing price into an intentional ritual.

apps.business_model: A digital memorial / ancestral-tribute shrine on MiniAppMemorialShrine (testnet 0x87f0fe2b..., mainnet 0xee7a548b..., verified ABI). A CREATOR makes a FREE on-chain memorial for a deceased loved one (name, photo hash/URL, relationship, birth/death years, biography, obituary). VISITORS pay a fixed-price GAS 'offering' to leave a tribute message: Incense 0.01 / Candle 0.02 / Flowers 0.03 / Fruit 0.05 / Wine 0.10 / Feast 0.50 GAS (confirmed via getOfferingMenu/getOfferingCost). payTribute records the offering (TributePaid) and increments per-memorial offering tallies; tribute messages + the offering type are permanent on-chain. Memorials with obituaries surface in a 'Recent Obituaries' feed. Who-pays-whom: visitor → contract (the offering GAS is held by the contract; there is NO per-creator payout method in the ABI and NO refund — it is a sunk donation to the shrine, NOT income to the deceased's family). The app brands itself 'Non-Profit — fees only cover blockchain costs.'
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Browse the memorial grid + obituary banner (loads from getMemorialCount/getMemorialDetails/getRecentObituaries). 2) CREATE (free): tap Create Memorial → fill name/photo/relationship/years/bio/obituary → createMemorial (no GAS) → MemorialCreated → memorial appears. 3) VISIT: open a memorial (tracked locally as Visited) → view bio + offerings received. 4) TRIBUTE: pick an offering (cost shown), write a message → payTribute prepays the fixed cost (memo miniapp-memorial-shrine:tribute:...) → TributePaid → tally increments, 'My Tributes' grows. 5) Share a memorial link so others can pay tribute. No exit/withdraw — offerings are donations.

gaps.title: 'Non-Profit — fees only cover blockchain costs' is misleading vs. the 0.01–0.50 GAS offering prices
gaps.evidence: feature2Name/feature2Desc (locale/messages.ts:32-33) claim 'Non-Profit' / 'Fees only cover blockchain costs.' But offering prices scale 0.01→0.50 GAS by ceremony tier (incense vs feast), which is a SYMBOLIC pricing ladder, not a gas-cost passthrough (a NEP-17 transfer + write costs roughly the same regardless of offering type). The contract holds the offering GAS with no creator payout and no refund (verified: no withdraw/payout method). So the 'fees only cover blockchain costs' line is not accurate and the destination of the GAS (held by the contract/platform, not the family) is never disclosed before a visitor pays up to 0.5 GAS.
gaps.fix: Replace the inaccurate 'fees only cover blockchain costs' copy with an honest statement of the model: 'Offerings are symbolic on-chain tributes. The GAS is not paid to the family; it is consumed as a permanent record of your tribute.' Surface this once near the offering selector (PlayArea.tsx:267-296). Frontend copy only — do not claim non-profit.

gaps.title: Tribute panel doesn't disclose the offering GAS is non-refundable and not received by anyone
gaps.evidence: The tribute form shows the offering cost (PlayArea.tsx:277-280) but no statement that the payment is a one-way, non-refundable on-chain record (the contract neither refunds nor routes it to the memorial creator — confirmed no payout method). A visitor selecting 'Feast · 0.50 GAS' has no way to know whether that GAS goes to the family, the platform, or is sunk.
gaps.fix: Add a one-line note under the offering cost card: 'Tributes are permanent and non-refundable; the offering is recorded on-chain, not transferred to anyone.' Frontend copy only.

apps.business_model: A private, wallet-scoped photo album that lives ENTIRELY ON-DEVICE (no contract — manifest contracts:{}). The user (someone wanting a quick private gallery tied to their wallet identity) saves up to 5 small images (≤60KB total per batch) into browser localStorage keyed by their connected wallet address, with optional client-side AES-GCM encryption (password never leaves the device). There is NO economic model: no GAS, no transaction, no on-chain write, no fee — it is a free utility. Identity-only use of the chain: the wallet address is the album's namespace, so switching wallets switches albums. Custody/risk: photos persist across reloads but do NOT sync across devices and are NOT backed up or on-chain — clearing browser storage loses them. The app is honest about this in current copy.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Connect wallet (album is scoped to its address). 2) Choose up to 5 images, keep total <60KB (live meter). 3) Optionally toggle Encrypt + set a password (AES-GCM, local). 4) Upload → saved to this device's localStorage under the wallet address — no wallet prompt, no GAS. 5) View public photos inline; encrypted photos require entering the password to decrypt locally. 6) Delete removes from device. No money lifecycle; the only 'exit' is local delete.

gaps.title: Name + 'Forever'/'永久' branding contradict the device-local, non-backed-up reality
gaps.evidence: The product is named 'Forever Album' / '永久相册' (manifest, locale/messages.ts:4,114) and the category is on-chain social, which strongly implies permanent/cloud/on-chain durability. The actual model (useForeverAlbum.ts:1-26) is browser localStorage that 'won't appear on another device or browser' and is lost if storage is cleared. The body copy is honest (vaultHeroSubtitle, localStorageNote, docDescription all say device-local, no sync), but the NAME promises permanence the storage cannot deliver — a user trusting the 'Forever' framing could lose irreplaceable photos when they clear their browser or switch devices.
gaps.fix: Lead the hero with a durability disclaimer prominent enough to override the name, e.g. a small warning chip near the title: 'Saved only on this device — back up originals elsewhere; clearing your browser deletes them.' (Name is fixed by manifest, but the hero/empty-state copy is frontend-editable.) Optionally reframe the subtitle to 'A private album on THIS device' as the dominant message.

gaps.title: Leftover on-chain/transaction strings imply a paid upload that no longer exists
gaps.evidence: The locale still carries dead on-chain-era strings that contradict the local-only model: 'imageTooLarge: Image too large for on-chain limit' (messages.ts:62), 'totalTooLarge: Total size exceeds the transaction limit' (messages.ts:63), 'readyToSign: Ready to sign the wallet upload' (messages.ts:44), 'storageKernelUnavailable' / 'missingContract' / lastTransaction/transactionPending (messages.ts:45-47,58-61,75). uploadReadiness/size copy in PlayArea may surface 'transaction limit' wording even though uploadPhotos() never touches the chain (useForeverAlbum.ts:364-413). A user reading 'sign the wallet upload' or 'on-chain limit' expects a GAS prompt that never comes.
gaps.fix: Reword the user-facing size/limit and readiness strings to device terms: 'Image too large to store on this device', 'Total exceeds the per-batch size limit', drop 'sign the wallet upload' in favor of 'Save to this device'. Remove/neutralize the dead transaction/contract strings. Frontend copy only.

apps.business_model: A gamified engagement/loyalty app (manifest category 'games', tags rewards/daily/streak). User = any Neo wallet holder. Value: build a UTC-day check-in streak and earn GAS at milestones. Economic model (verified on-chain, mainnet 0xbd4f3646 and testnet 0xaba84da2 via getPlatformStats): each check-in is a deposit-then-act GAS transfer of checkInFee=100000 base units (0.001 GAS) carrying memo 'miniapp-dailycheckin:checkin'; OnNEP17Payment records the streak and accrues a milestone reward — weekReward=1 GAS at day 7, twoWeekReward=2 GAS at day 14, then resetAfterDays=14 cycles the streak. claimRewards(user) pays the accrued GAS to the user FROM THE CONTRACT'S OWN BALANCE (the contract is the reward pool). So the user pays ~0.001 GAS/day (≈0.014 GAS over a 14-day cycle) for the chance to claim 3 GAS — net the house funds the rewards. Whoever funds the contract bears the payout cost.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → see streak/next-reward/fee in hero → once per UTC day, Check In (deposit 0.001 GAS fee, OnNEP17Payment records streak, emits CheckedIn) → at day 7 a 1 GAS reward accrues (unclaimed), day 14 +2 GAS, then streak resets → Claim Rewards (direct claimRewards call, contract transfers accrued GAS out) anytime → countdown to next UTC midnight gates the next check-in. Recovery: there is no deposited principal to withdraw (the fee is spent); rewards are pull-claimed when funded.

gaps.title: Advertised GAS rewards are unfunded on the live contract; UI never shows reward-pool solvency
gaps.evidence: Hero (PlayArea.tsx:125) and locale (messages.ts feature2Desc/docDescription) prominently promise 'Day 7: 1 GAS, Day 14: 2 GAS', and a 'Claim Rewards' button is always shown (PlayArea.tsx:204-209). But claimRewards pays from the contract's own balance (useCheckin.ts:649-655 'the contract pays the accrued reward to the user from its own balance'). Live read: mainnet contract 0xbd4f3646 holds only 1,500,000 base units = 0.015 GAS, while one day-7 reward is 1 GAS (1e8) — ~66x short. getPlatformStats().totalRewarded = 0 on BOTH mainnet and testnet (1870 testnet check-ins, 15 mainnet), i.e. no user has ever successfully claimed a reward, consistent with an empty pool. A newcomer pays 0.001 GAS/day expecting GAS they cannot actually claim.
gaps.fix: Read the contract's GAS balance (chain.read 'balanceOf' on GAS_HASH with the contract scriptHash) and getPlatformStats().totalRewarded, and surface a 'Reward pool' fact in the hero / Today-plan card. When pool balance < the next milestone reward (weekReward/twoWeekReward already read in getPlatformStats), show a 'Rewards currently unfunded — check-in still records your streak' banner and disable/relabel the Claim button when unclaimed>0 but pool is insufficient, so the value-prop is honest. Frontend-only over existing reads.

gaps.title: Contract pause state (isPaused) has no UI; check-in/claim silently fault when paused
gaps.evidence: The deployed ABI exposes isPaused() and pauseRegistry()/setPaused (getcontractstate on 0xaba84da2). The frontend never reads isPaused (useCheckin.ts reads only getCheckInStateForFrontend/getCheckinStatus/getUserStatsDetails/getPlatformStats). If an admin pauses the app, the Check In CTA still renders 'Check In Now' and the user's tx faults with a raw error instead of a clear 'temporarily paused' state.
gaps.fix: Add a chain.read('isPaused', []) to loadAll; when true, replace the check-in CTA label with a localized 'Check-in paused' state and disable Check In / Claim, mirroring the existing hasLoadedStatus gating in PlayArea.tsx:84-89.

gaps.title: Copy promises 'collectible badge progress' but no badges are shown
gaps.evidence: docDescription (messages.ts:46) says streak resets 'with collectible badge progress intact' and the contract has getUserBadgeCount(user)/hasBadge(user,badgeType) plus DailyBadgeEarned / MilestoneReached events (ABI). The UI renders only a milestone GAS ladder and recent history — no badge count or badge collection anywhere in PlayArea.tsx. The promised collectible-badge mechanic is illegible.
gaps.fix: Either drop the 'collectible badge progress' phrasing from docDescription, or read getUserBadgeCount(user) and surface a small 'Badges earned: N' stat in the meta strip (PlayArea.tsx:267) so the copy maps to a visible artifact.

apps.business_model: A bridge PREPARATION console (manifest category 'defi', description 'Prepare official Neo N3 / Neo X bridge handoffs and track operation status'). User = someone who wants to move GAS (or send a cross-chain message) between Neo N3 and Neo X. Critically, contracts:{} is empty — this app moves NO funds and signs NOTHING. Its 'product' is to validate inputs (direction, amount, target-chain address) and emit a deterministic JSON 'handoff intent' + a non-cryptographic FNV digest the user then executes on the OFFICIAL BaneLabs/AxLabs bridge (xbridge.neo.org / testnet bridge). The 'Track' tab renders a LOCAL, fabricated 5-step lifecycle from form state, not real on-chain probing. No fees, no custody, no payouts on this app — all economic value/risk lives in the external bridge the user is handed off to.
apps.intended_workflow: Pick mode (Asset / Message / Track) → for Asset: choose direction, GAS amount, validated target-chain recipient → Prepare asset handoff → app outputs a JSON intent + digest + a timeline preview → user copies the payload and goes to the official bridge app to actually sign+submit the source tx → returns to Track tab, pastes the source tx hash to advance the local timeline preview. There is no on-chain state owned by this app; 'exit/recovery' is entirely on the external bridge.

gaps.title: Console never tells the user the bridge happens ELSEWHERE — the prepared payload looks like a completed/executable action
gaps.evidence: After preparing, the user sees 'Generated bridge handoff' (appConfig.ts outputTitle), a digest, an operation id (N3X-ASSET-...), and a 5-step 'Operation status' timeline ending in 'Destination chain releases or mints the bridged GAS' (bridgeConsole.ts:362-366). Nothing in the hero/output/timeline states that NO transaction was sent and that the user must now go execute it on the official bridge app. heroBody (appConfig.ts:311) says 'Prepare official bridge handoff payloads ... and preview the cross-chain lifecycle' but a first-timer who entered an amount + recipient and clicked 'Prepare asset handoff' can reasonably believe their GAS is now bridging. The resource links to the real bridge are a quiet row at the bottom (PlayArea.tsx:702-707), not positioned as the required next step.
gaps.fix: Add an explicit 'Next step' affordance directly under the generated payload: a primary 'Open official bridge to submit' button linking to bridgeAppTestnet/Mainnet plus copy like 'This console only prepares the handoff — paste this into the official bridge and sign there to actually move funds.' Add a one-line disclaimer in the hero/output card ('No funds move from this console'). Frontend-only copy + reorder of the existing BRIDGE_RESOURCES link.

gaps.title: Prepared handoff is hardcoded to testnet even on mainnet routes; digest is called 'signed' but nothing is signed
gaps.evidence: buildAssetBridgeIntent hardcodes environment:'testnet' and resources.bridgeApp:BRIDGE_RESOURCES.bridgeAppTestnet (bridgeConsole.ts:204,211) regardless of the manifest's mainnet support (neo-manifest supported_networks includes neo-x-mainnet/neo-n3-mainnet). A mainnet user gets a payload labeled 'testnet' pointing at the testnet bridge. Separately, emptyPayloadHint (appConfig.ts:222-224) says the panel will 'generate the signed bridge handoff', and stableDigest (bridgeConsole.ts:149-165) is a 64-bit FNV/imul hash — not a signature and not chain-verifiable. Calling an unsigned local hash a 'signed handoff' misrepresents what the user is holding.
gaps.fix: Derive environment + resources.bridgeApp from the active launch network instead of the testnet literal, and point the bottom resource link to the mainnet bridge when on mainnet. Reword emptyPayloadHint/output copy from 'signed bridge handoff' to 'prepared bridge intent' and label the digest as a 'local reference digest (not a signature)'. Frontend-only.

gaps.title: 'Track Operation' implies live status but only animates a local form-derived timeline
gaps.evidence: The Track tab and manifest op 'trackBridgeOperation' (neo-manifest.json) read as a real status lookup ('Track a lock, relay, or release transaction'), but buildStatusTimeline (bridgeConsole.ts:306-371) sets step states purely from whether the user typed an operationId/sourceTx — it never queries the chain or the bridge relayer. Entering any 64-hex string flips 'Source transaction' to done. The user cannot distinguish a real bridge state from a cosmetic one.
gaps.fix: Relabel the Track tab/copy to 'Lifecycle preview' (opTrackDesc already hedges with 'local lifecycle') and add a one-line note that real status must be confirmed on the official bridge explorer, with a link. If feasible, link the entered sourceTx to a chain explorer for the source network so the user can independently verify the one fact that is real (the source tx). Frontend-only.

apps.business_model: A user-facing console (manifest category 'data') to define price-triggered automation 'recipes': read a NEO/GAS/BTC price from the on-chain MorpheusDataFeed, set a target price + cron schedule + an action (e.g. auto_repay_self_loan, rebalance_vault, claim_rewards, notify_webhook), and register the trigger with the host Morpheus automation gateway so an off-chain keeper executes it on schedule. User = a DeFi user who wants hands-off upkeep. There is no contract (contracts:{}) and no fee surfaced — the value is the executor running the action; who pays the execution gas / whether this is a paid keeper service is not modeled anywhere. Registration posts to /api/edge/automation-triggers; when that gateway is unavailable it degrades to a 'local_automation_intent' handoff that NEVER executes.
apps.intended_workflow: Read pricefeed (Fetch Price) → Build Recipe (validate target price + 5-field cron, assemble payload) → Register Trigger (POST to gateway → returns a verified trigger that the keeper will run, OR a local handoff intent) → operate verified triggers via Enable/Disable/Delete and watch Next Execution. The honest 3-step route is shown (routePrice/routeRegister/routeOperate). Exit = delete the trigger.

gaps.title: Registration almost always degrades to a non-executing 'handoff intent' but the UI doesn't explain the automation won't actually run
gaps.evidence: registerTrigger POSTs to /api/edge/automation-triggers (automationGateway.ts:175); per the platform's dead Morpheus edge this returns local_automation_intent, so latestTriggerState becomes 'Host handoff prepared' and Enable/Disable are locked (useAutomationCopilot.ts:215-219, PlayArea.tsx:66-67, verifyBeforeOperate note). The honest hint exists (automationGatewayHint), but a first-timer sees 'Host handoff prepared' with a Next-Execution row and a copyable payload and cannot tell that NO keeper will ever fire this trigger — the core promise (scheduled execution) silently doesn't happen. There is no 'executor unavailable / not scheduled' state distinct from a healthy registered trigger.
gaps.fix: When isLocalAutomationIntent is true, render an explicit status card: 'Automation executor unavailable — this recipe is saved as a draft and will NOT run on schedule.' Suppress or grey the 'Next Execution' row for handoff-only triggers (PlayArea.tsx:246-249 currently shows it) so it doesn't imply a scheduled run. Frontend-only over existing registration_state.

gaps.title: Current Price shown with no staleness/source freshness — the trigger condition can rest on a frozen feed
gaps.evidence: The hero shows 'Current Price' from on-chain MorpheusDataFeed (useAutomationCopilot.ts:108-123) with no timestamp or staleness check; per platform memory the MorpheusDataFeed price is frozen (last update 2026-03-09). A price-threshold trigger ('NEO gte 20') built against a frozen feed is meaningless, but the UI presents the price as live ('Live Inputs', feature1Desc). The user commits a recipe on data they cannot tell is stale.
gaps.fix: If the datafeed read exposes a timestamp/round, surface 'as of <time>' next to Current Price and warn when older than a threshold; if no timestamp is available, soften 'Live Inputs' copy to 'On-chain feed (verify freshness)' and add a caption that the trigger fires only when an executor re-reads the feed. Frontend-only over the existing datafeed read.

gaps.title: No cost/economic model for automation execution
gaps.evidence: The product implies a keeper runs the action on schedule (action.type 'morpheus_workflow', route '/automation/execute'), but nothing in the UI or copy states who pays the execution gas, whether the service is free/paid, or any limits. A user registering 'auto_repay_self_loan' on an hourly cron has no idea what it costs or whether funds/allowances are needed for the action to succeed.
gaps.fix: Add a short 'How execution works' note in the builder hint area (PlayArea.tsx:220) clarifying that the host keeper executes the action and that the target action (e.g. self-loan repay) must have funds/permissions in place; state the cost model (free preview / keeper-funded / requires the user's session key) honestly. Copy-only.

apps.business_model: A free, read-only Neo N3 block explorer (manifest category 'tools'). User = anyone wanting to look up chain data without signing. Value: search a tx hash / address / contract / block height against mainnet or testnet, see live network height + tx count + a recent-tx feed. No wallet, no fees, no custody, no economic model — it explicitly never requests signatures or sends assets (explorerSafetyDesc). Data comes from the n3index/explorer API.
apps.intended_workflow: Open → see live network stats (height, tx count, recent txs) for the selected network → paste an identifier → Search → result card renders the matched block/tx/address/contract, with type-aware not-found handling → tap a recent tx to inspect it. Read-only; no money lifecycle.

gaps.title: No link out to a canonical full explorer to verify the complete record
gaps.evidence: The product's value is verification, and SearchResultDisplay.tsx renders a trimmed projection (e.g. tx shows only hash/block/time/sender; contract shows name/methods/updateCounter/indexedCalls). There is no 'open in full explorer' link to the canonical chain explorer for the full transaction/contract record, so a user who needs the complete on-chain detail (transfers, notifications, full ABI) hits a dead end inside the miniapp.
gaps.fix: Add a small 'View full record ↗' link on each result card to a canonical Neo N3 explorer (e.g. the n3index web UI or neotube) for the matched identifier + network. Frontend-only, additive; does not change the read-only model.

apps.business_model: A free wallet safety self-assessment tool (manifest category 'tools', description 'Checklist and safety insights for your Neo wallet'). User = a Neo holder wanting a quick health check. Value: read live NEO/GAS balances on-chain (auto), then work a 6-item security checklist (backup phrase, keep GAS, review app permissions, trusted device, hardware wallet, 2FA) to compute a checklist-based Safety Score and risk band, with next-step recommendations and a downloadable/copyable report. No wallet writes, no fees, no custody. Only the 'Keep GAS for fees' item is auto-evaluated from the on-chain GAS balance; the other five are user-attested checkboxes stored device-locally.
apps.intended_workflow: Connect wallet → live NEO/GAS balances + auto GAS check populate → tick off the manual checklist items (saved locally) → Safety Score / risk chip update → read recommendations → copy address / copy or download the health report. Revisit periodically. No money lifecycle to recover.

gaps.title: Safety Score can read as an on-chain security analysis when it is mostly self-attested
gaps.evidence: The hero shows a big numeric ring + risk chip labeled 'Wallet Health' with no inline note that 5 of 6 inputs are self-reported checkboxes (useHealthScore.ts:58-94 — only 'gas' is auto). A newcomer can read a '83% / Low risk' score as 'the app analyzed my wallet and it's safe'. The honest framing exists but is buried (feature2Desc 'Checklist-based score', connectHint 'checklist stays local'), not adjacent to the score ring (PlayArea.tsx:140-160).
gaps.fix: Add a one-line caption under the score ring (alongside the existing connectToScore caption slot, PlayArea.tsx:150-152) like 'Self-assessment score — based on your checklist, not an on-chain audit.' Copy-only.

gaps.title: 'Review app permissions / revoke approvals' recommendation has no way to actually inspect on-chain approvals
gaps.evidence: The checklist + recommendations push 'Audit dApp permissions and revoke unused approvals' (messages.ts recommendationPermissions, checklistPermissionsDesc) as a tickable item, but the app reads only NEO/GAS balanceOf (useWalletAnalysis.ts:54-65) and provides no view of the wallet's actual approvals/sessions. The user is asked to attest to an action the tool gives them no means to perform or verify, which makes that item feel hollow.
gaps.fix: Either reframe the item as pure guidance ('Check approvals in your wallet app') with a link to where the user can manage them, or add a 'How to review approvals' tip. Copy/link-only; no contract change.

apps.business_model: A DEVELOPER TOOL, not a transacting app: neo-manifest.json category=tools, contracts:{}, transactions:false, walletRequired:false. The user is a dApp builder who wants to compose a Morpheus confidential-compute request (workflow=risk-score|proof-check|batch-transform, privacy=sealed|public, a JSON input payload) and inspect its deterministic decoded shape + a local FNV digest BEFORE that request is dispatched to the Morpheus compute lane from another surface. No money changes hands; the only 'economic' fact is that actual dispatch/execution requires a Morpheus runtime token (the panel's preview-only notice). Value: a safe, sealed-input-redacting preview surface so a team can review exactly what compute request they intend to bind on-chain (payload.execution='preview_only', dispatchReady:false). buildResult validates the JSON input and, in sealed mode, replaces the raw input with '[sealed input redacted]' in the visible payload.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Pick a workflow + privacy mode + paste a JSON input. 2) Click 'Build Preview' -> the panel shows status (ready / 'Enter a valid JSON input payload'), summary, a rows table (workflow, privacy, input-valid yes/no, input digest, full digest), and an expandable JSON payload card. 3) Sealed mode keeps raw input out of the visible payload (inputPreview redacted). 4) User copies the payload JSON and carries the digest to the real Morpheus dispatch step (which needs a runtime token). There is no on-chain state, no funds, no settlement here — exit is simply copying the package; Reset restores the seeded placeholders. The shared panel's 'Preview only — dispatching requires a Morpheus runtime token' notice is the honest end-of-lifecycle marker.

gaps.title: Hero stat 'Network: Morpheus Mainnet' implies a live connection the preview never makes
gaps.evidence: appConfig.ts resolveNetworkLabel() returns 'Morpheus Mainnet' (comment: 'the actually-live lane the console opened on') and binds it to the hero statNetwork stat (manifest stats[0]). But buildResult only computes a local FNV digest (previewId) with payload.execution='preview_only', dispatchReady:false — nothing touches the network. A first-timer reading 'Network: Morpheus Mainnet' + a green 'Compute preview ready' status reasonably concludes the request was sent to mainnet, when the app is a pure offline builder.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: relabel the hero stat from 'Network' to 'Target lane' / 'Dispatch target' (change statNetwork label key usage or the value text to e.g. 'Morpheus Mainnet (not yet dispatched)'), and/or add a short copy line under the hero referencing the preview-only notice so the network label reads as the intended destination, not a completed call.

gaps.title: Value prop for a newcomer: 'why build a preview I can't dispatch here?' is not answered up-front
gaps.evidence: panelDescription says 'Shape compute work into a deterministic preview' and the only outbound affordance is 'Copy' the payload. The shared notice 'Preview only — dispatching requires a Morpheus runtime token' (ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:281, consolePreviewNotice) explains WHY but not WHAT NEXT — a developer cannot tell where the copied payload + digest actually get used (which contract/SDK/dispatch surface consumes it).
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: extend the docs[] features copy (feature3Desc 'Dispatch Aware') or the panelDescription to name the downstream consumer concretely (e.g. 'Copy this package into your Morpheus dispatch call / submitMiniAppRequest — the digest lets you confirm the bound request matches'). This makes the builder's role in the larger flow legible.

apps.business_model: A DEVELOPER TOOL (category=tools, contracts:{}, transactions:false): the user composes an HTTP oracle read for Morpheus — method (GET/POST), URL, a JSONPath extraction path, optional POST body — and inspects the decoded request + local digest before it is bound to an on-chain callback. Value: catch a malformed URL or JSONPath typo (the config validates http(s) scheme + a lightweight JSONPath grammar) BEFORE the request is committed on-chain, and produce an auditable digest so teams can compare 'intended request' vs 'submitted request' (feature3 'Auditable'). No funds; dispatch requires a Morpheus runtime token. The seeded default URL points at the live mainnet worker's /health (DEFAULT_HTTP_URL = morpheusPublicApiUrl + '/health').
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Choose method, enter URL + JSONPath (+ body for POST). 2) Click 'Preview Request' -> status ('HTTP request ready' / 'Enter a valid http(s) URL' / 'Enter a valid JSON path (start with $)'), rows (method, URL, URL-valid, path, path-valid, digest), JSON payload (kind oracle.http.request). 3) Copy the payload; carry the digest to the on-chain callback binding step (needs runtime token). No on-chain state/funds here; Reset clears.

gaps.title: The seeded default URL is a live, reachable Morpheus endpoint, but the console never offers to actually call it — even though the worker serves it tokenlessly
gaps.evidence: DEFAULT_HTTP_URL seeds the field with the live mainnet worker (oracle.meshmini.app/mainnet/health). ConsoleToolPanel exposes an opt-in execute() hook (lines 70-86) whose own comment confirms the worker 'serves tokenless GETs for feeds/price/:symbol, feeds/catalog, neodid/providers and oracle/public-key'. This console wires only buildResult, never execute, so a user who enters a GET to a tokenless lane still only gets a local digest and the 'Preview only' notice — the product's promise ('compare intended vs submitted request') is half-realized: you can build but never see a real response to compare against.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: wire config.execute for GET requests to the documented tokenless GET lanes (fetch the URL, surface HTTP status + the JSONPath-extracted value as result rows). Keep POST / non-allowlisted hosts as preview-only with the existing notice. This turns the 'Auditable / compare' value prop into something the user can actually do for read lanes without a token.

gaps.title: 'Network: Morpheus Mainnet' hero stat is misleading for an offline builder
gaps.evidence: Same pattern as compute-lab: resolveNetworkLabel() binds 'Morpheus Mainnet' to the hero statNetwork while buildResult does no network I/O. Paired with a green 'HTTP request ready', a newcomer may think the HTTP read executed.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: relabel to 'Target lane' / append '(preview)' to the network value, or (preferably, combined with the execute() fix above) keep the live label honest by actually executing tokenless GETs.

apps.business_model: A DEVELOPER TOOL (category=tools, contracts:{}, transactions:false): the user composes a NeoDID identity-verification request for Morpheus — a did:neo subject, a provider (registry/wallet-signature/social-attestation), a claim (e.g. profile.kyc), and an optional hash160 callback contract — and previews the decoded verification package + digest before Morpheus dispatch. Value: validate the DID shape and callback-hash format and produce a reviewable package so an identity request can be audited before it is bound to an on-chain callback (payload kind oracle.neodid.verify, execution preview_only). No funds; dispatch needs a runtime token.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Enter DID + claim (required), pick provider, optional callback hash. 2) 'Preview Verification' -> status (required-fields / 'Enter a valid did:neo identifier' / 'Callback must be a 0x hash160' / ready), rows (DID, DID-valid, provider, claim, callback-valid?, digest), JSON payload. 3) Copy package + carry digest to dispatch. No on-chain state/funds; Reset clears.

gaps.title: Provider list is a hardcoded 3-option fiction; the live Morpheus NeoDID provider catalog is different and tokenlessly readable
gaps.evidence: appConfig.ts hardcodes provider options neodid-registry / wallet-signature / social-attestation. The live mainnet worker's GET /neodid/providers (confirmed tokenless, returns {providers:[{id:'web3auth',category:'identity',claim_types:['Web3Auth_PrimaryIdentity',...]},{id:'twitter',...},{id:'github',...}...]}) exposes the ACTUAL provider ids + claim_types Morpheus accepts. A developer who builds a request selecting 'neodid-registry' / claim 'profile.kyc' is composing a request that does not correspond to any real provider/claim the oracle recognizes — the preview looks valid but is semantically wrong, defeating the 'reviewable before dispatch' promise.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: fetch GET {morpheusPublicApiUrl}/neodid/providers on load (tokenless) and populate the provider select from the real catalog; optionally constrain/suggest the claim field from the selected provider's claim_types. Fall back to the static list only if the fetch fails. This makes the previewed request match what Morpheus will actually verify.

gaps.title: Default DID is a testnet sample ('did:neo:testnet:sample-user') even though the console defaults to the mainnet lane
gaps.evidence: DEFAULT_DID = 'did:neo:testnet:sample-user' while resolveNetworkLabel() and default_network are mainnet. A first-timer building a 'mainnet' verification preview starts from a testnet-namespaced sample DID, an internal contradiction in the seeded example.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: seed the default DID to match the launched network (did:neo:mainnet:sample-user on mainnet) via getNetwork(), mirroring resolveNetworkLabel().

gaps.title: Network hero stat implies a live verification call the preview never makes
gaps.evidence: Hero binds statNetwork to 'Morpheus Mainnet' (statEndpoint 'NeoDID verifier') while buildResult only computes a local digest. 'NeoDID verifier' + 'Verification preview ready' can read as 'identity verified'.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: relabel statEndpoint/value to make 'preview-only' explicit (e.g. 'Mode: Preview builder') or append a clarifier to the network value.

apps.business_model: The one genuinely-transacting (read-only) console: an operator/dev tool that reads asset prices DIRECTLY from the deployed on-chain MorpheusDataFeed contract via Neo N3 JSON-RPC (usePriceConsole -> useMorpheusDataFeed.getPriceWithMeta), with no off-chain HTTP/edge dependency. Value: a fast, trustless price lookup (NEO/GAS/BTC + the on-chain listPairs catalog) that surfaces the feed contract hash (copyable) and an explicit freshness badge so a frozen feed is never shown as live (STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS=1h, the guard that hid a 3-month testnet freeze). No funds; the 'economic truth' the product promises is the canonical on-chain price + its staleness.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) On load, fetchPrice() reads the current asset from the on-chain feed and loadPairs() extends the asset select from the on-chain catalog. 2) User picks an asset -> 'Fetch Price' -> the price card shows $price, a freshness pill (fresh '…updated Xm ago' / stale 'last update Xd ago' + a stale hint banner), the feed contract hash (truncated, click to copy full), network, source ('on-chain {network} RPC'). 3) Errors map to stable messages (not-deployed/timeout/fault/network). Exit: read the price + verify the feed hash on an explorer. Fully self-contained, no dispatch step.

gaps.title: Freshness is shown but the absolute on-chain timestamp / block is not surfaced for verification
gaps.evidence: usePriceConsole reads quote.dataTimestamp/recordTimestamp and renders only a relative 'Xm ago' label (formatRelativeAge). The product promises an inspectable, trustless feed read and even makes the contract hash copyable, but a user cannot see the exact timestamp the feed wrote (only 'fresh/stale'), which is the precise datum needed to independently verify freshness against the chain.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add the absolute timestamp (ISO/local time from lastTimestamp) as a small caption or title tooltip on the freshness pill, and/or expose it in the sidebar. The value is already fetched; only display is missing.

apps.business_model: A DEVELOPER TOOL (category=tools, contracts:{}, transactions:false): the user packages a sensitive oracle input (purpose=oracle-input|callback-secret|attestation, optional recipient/route, a private JSON payload) into an 'envelope preview' with a stable NON-cryptographic reference checksum, intended as a pre-dispatch organizing surface. Round-2 copy was corrected to state plainly that the checksum 'is not encryption' / 'not encrypted, hidden, or tamper-proof' (feature1Desc). Value: a way to give a sensitive request a stable reference id and explicit envelope version (morpheus-seal-v1) before it is sent to Morpheus confidential handling. No funds; dispatch needs a runtime token.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Pick purpose, optional recipient, paste private JSON payload. 2) 'Build Envelope' -> status ('Envelope preview ready' / 'Preview ready (payload is not valid JSON)'), rows (purpose, recipient or '—', payload-valid, payload checksum, full checksum), payload (kind oracle.seal.envelope, envelopeVersion morpheus-seal-v1). 3) Copy the envelope; carry the checksum to the real seal/dispatch step. No on-chain state/funds; Reset clears.

gaps.title: App is named/branded 'Seal' and packages a 'Sensitive Payload' but performs NO sealing — the real sealing public key is live and tokenless yet unused
gaps.evidence: manifest name 'Oracle Seal Console', icon 'locked', neo-manifest operation 'Seal Payload' (sensitive:true) / 'Encrypt a sensitive payload for Morpheus confidential handling'. The actual code (appConfig.buildResult) only JSON-validates the payload and computes previewId() (an FNV-1a non-crypto hash) — the raw payload is even echoed back in the copyable payload object's not-redacted (only the checksum is shown, but the payload textarea content is the user's and is summarized, not protected). The live worker's GET /oracle/public-key returns a real X25519-HKDF-SHA256-AES-256-GCM key with key_source:'nitro-sealed' and recommended_payload_encryption — i.e. real client-side sealing IS possible tokenlessly, but the console ignores it. Despite the corrected feature copy, the app NAME, lock icon, 'Seal Payload', and 'Sensitive Payload' label still strongly imply protection the tool does not provide.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only, pick one: (a) actually fetch /oracle/public-key (tokenless) and surface it + the algorithm so the user can see/verify the real sealing key the envelope targets (and optionally perform WebCrypto X25519 sealing of the payload, replacing the FNV checksum); OR (b) if sealing stays out of scope, harden the framing — retitle the panel/field from 'Sensitive Payload'/'Seal' toward 'request envelope reference' and add a prominent inline warning that the payload is NOT encrypted by this tool, so the lock branding does not over-promise.

gaps.title: 'Sealed/private' indigo theme + lock icon set a privacy mental model the checksum does not deliver
gaps.evidence: appConfig comment explicitly chose accentColor #4f46e5 so the console 'reads as private input'. Combined with the locked icon and 'Build Envelope', a first-time user reasonably believes their pasted secret is being protected; in reality it is only checksummed and is included in the copyable JSON. The corrected feature1Desc text is the only counter-signal and is buried in docs, not next to the payload field.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: put the 'not encrypted / reference only' disclaimer directly adjacent to the payload textarea (placeholder or helper text) and/or on the result status, not only in docs, so the privacy framing is corrected at the point of input.

apps.business_model: A DEVELOPER TOOL (category=tools, contracts:{}, transactions:false): the user composes a Morpheus verifiable-randomness (VRF) request — consumer (a MiniApp contract hash / app id), a salt (unique per round/campaign), a rounds count (clamped 1-10), and a proof mode (single/batch) — and previews the request with a deterministic client-side request id before submission. Value: a tuned form for game rounds / raffles / randomized flows (feature2 'Game Ready') that produces an unambiguous request id binding consumer+salt+rounds+mode so the eventual on-chain VRF draw can be matched to the intended request. No funds; the live vrf/random lane is gated behind Turnstile/token so this stays preview-only.
apps.intended_workflow: 1) Enter consumer + salt (required), set rounds (1-10, silently clamped with an 'adjusted' row when out of range), pick proof mode. 2) 'Build VRF Request' -> status ('VRF request ready' / 'Required fields missing'), rows (consumer, salt, rounds, [rounds-adjusted], client digest = request id), payload kind oracle.vrf.request. 3) Copy package + carry the request id to the real VRF submission (needs token). hideRequestCount:true because the local tally isn't a draw count. No on-chain state/funds; Reset clears.

gaps.title: The request id is presented as the verification handle, but the console never explains that VRF verification (the product's whole point) happens elsewhere/later
gaps.evidence: The product is 'verifiable randomness': the value is that the eventual draw comes with a proof. The console builds a request id (previewId of consumer|salt|rounds|mode) and labels feature3 'Proof Aware', but there is no UI for the second half of the lifecycle — submitting the request, receiving randomness, and verifying the proof. The 'Preview only — dispatching requires a Morpheus runtime token' notice (shared) is the only hint, and it doesn't tell a game dev where the draw/proof is obtained or how the request id maps to it.
gaps.fix: Frontend-only: add copy (panelDescription or feature3Desc) that completes the loop — 'this request id is what you submit to the Morpheus VRF lane / your consumer contract; the returned proof can be matched back to this id'. Optionally link to the consumer-contract VRF pattern. No contract change; just makes the request->draw->verify lifecycle legible.
